label: 1862 Peaceful Way
request: Request approval of Waiver from Land Development Regulations Section 155.047, and approval of Sketch Plan for subdivision on Peaceful Way of three SF residential Lots zoned R-1, Low Density Residential District, located at 1862 Peaceful Way. TMS No.: 556-00-00-280; 556-00-00-490

events.text:
Mr. McNeill recused himself due to a conflict of interest. Planning Commission

Mr. Mitchell reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2).

Ms. Smith asked if the trust is currently undeveloped. Mr. Mitchell answered that the information provided shows it is not developed. Ms. Smith asked if it could be developed. Mr. Mitchell answered that it is a lot of record and could be developed.

Ms. Campaigne asked about staff comment #8 and the planting plan and how enforcement would be handled. Mr. Mitchell answered that the Town would hold off on recording until the requirements were met. He stated that prior to the lots being established, all requirements would have to be met.

Mr. Neal asked if this would need to be a conditional approval. Mr. Pagliarini answered that conditions could be placed on the approval if desired by the Commission.

Mr. Kevin Berry, Earthsource Engineering, reviewed the request with the Commission. He stated that all encroachments into the critical line buffer would be removed.

Mr. Chapman asked about the main driveway and suggested that care should be taken when shifting the location of the driveway in order to better preserve the significant tree. Mr. Berry agreed.

Mr. Neal moved for approval of the request including all staff comments. Ms. Campaigne seconded the motion. Motion carried on a 7 to 1 vote with Ms. Campaigne, Ms. Gregg, Mr. Chapman, Mr. Wren, Mr. Millet, Mr. Neal, and Mr. Cuttino in favor; Ms. Smith opposed and Mr. McNeill abstaining.

label: 1480 & 1492 Rifle Range Road
request: Request approval of Preliminary Plat for Shell Landing Subdivision, 16 SF residential Lots zoned R-2, Single-family residential district, located at 1480 & 1492 Rifle Range Road. TMS No.: 560-06-00-025; 560-06-00-001

events.text:
Mr. Bernard reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2). Planning Commission

Mr. Neal asked if the fact that the tree survey is more than a year old would render the submittal incomplete. Mr. Bernard answered that the tree survey should not be more than one year old, but this project has been in progress for some time. Mr. Neal asked if the request should be deferred. Mr. Bernard answered that given the minimal time that has passed, the tree size would not be significantly different.

Ms. Campaigne asked if any of the 30 trees requested for removal would be of concern. Mr. Bernard answered that many of the trees not shown on the preliminary plat were shown on the sketch plan. Additionally, he stated that some of the building footprints have been changed from the sketch plan as well. He suggested that it appears that some of the trees requested for removal could be retained.

Mr. McNeill asked if staff has met with the applicant regarding the discrepancies. Mr. Bernard answered in the negative.

Mr. Millet asked if a SCDOT encroachment permit was approved. Mr. Bernard answered that the application indicates that SCDOT approval was received in August 2016.

Mr. Wren asked about tree mitigation. Mr. Bernard answered that there are several options including payment into the tree bank, a tree bond, planting in the HOA area, retention of trees, etc.

Mr. Chapman asked about sidewalks and why the sidewalks in Shell Landing were not extended. Mr. Bernard answered that the sidewalk would be retained with the exception of where the proposed access would be located. He stated that there would be a sidewalk on Rifle Range Road that connects to this development.

Mr. Matt Cline, Cline Engineering, reviewed the request with the Commission.

Ms. Smith asked the reason for the discrepancy between the sketch plan and the preliminary plat in regard to trees. Mr. Cline answered that there was a change in the requirements between the sketch plan approval and preliminary Planning Commission

plat request. He stated that additionally, it was determined that based on the grading and drainage plan, some additional trees would need to be removed.

Mr. Neal expressed concern with the number of trees being requested for removal that were not previously indicated with the sketch plan approval. Mr. Neal expressed additional concern with the number of trees being requested for removal within the proposed right-of-way. He suggested that the lots could be reconfigured in order to preserve additional trees.

Ms. Campaigne expressed concern with trees #22, #18, #33, #97, #103, and #92 and asked the reason for being removed. Mr. Cline answered that some of the trees are not protected, while others were in poor condition and reviewed these with the Commission.

Mr. Millet concurred with Ms. Campaigne’s concerns regarding the number of trees requested for removal. He asked about tree #17 and #32. Mr. Cline answered that #17 would be within the building footprint and would be below the roadway grade once the grading was completed. He stated that tree #32 is in good condition but requested for removal because of the amount of grading that would have to occur for that lot. Mr. Millet asked about tree #38. Mr. Cline answered that it is between two houses in a swale.

Mr. Neal suggested that a number of significant trees in good condition are proposed for removal and asked if this could be reviewed to determine if more trees could be preserved. Mr. Cline answered that the applicant has worked extensively with staff and asked that a decision be made on the request.

Ms. Gregg asked for clarification on what would be accomplished with “working with staff on the tree survey”. Mr. Cline answered that he was not a part of the project at the beginning and stated that he would like to have an opportunity to work with staff.

Ms. Smith moved for denial of the request. Mr. Wren seconded the motion.

Mr. Wren asked the difference between a deferral and denial of a preliminary plat. Mr. Pagliarini answered that the denial of the preliminary plat would mean the applicant would have to bring back a different project layout for approval. Planning Commission

Mr. Neal suggested that a deferral might be more appropriate in order for the applicant to have an opportunity to bring a different plan back for approval.

Ms. Campaigne suggested that there are a number of protected trees that are of concern and suggested that the concerns should be addressed before a decision is made. Ms. Smith and Mr. Wren agreed.

Mr. McNeill suggested that one reason for an updated tree survey is to provide information to address some of the concerns raised by the Commission. He suggested that the application should not have been brought to the Commission for consideration.

Mr. Chapman stated that the Commission has purview over the protection of trees. He stated that this is a concern and the Commission is sensitive to this issue. He suggested that having an opportunity restudy the plan and work with staff to better preserve the existing trees would be beneficial.

Mr. Chapman called for a vote on the motion. All in favor.

Mr. Wren left at this time (5:46 pm).

label: Location: Bessemer Road
request: Request approval of Sketch Plan for Bessemer Road Townhomes, 21 townhouse units zoned PD, Planned Development District, located at Location: Bessemer Road. TMS No.: 583-03-00-172; 583-03-00-177

events.text:
Ms. Salomon reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2).

Mr. Chapman asked the reason that there was no interconnectivity proposed between this project and Covington via Wagner Road. He suggested that if this could be accomplished, it could mean one less curb cut on Bessemer Road. Mr. Mitchell answered that interconnectivity from Covington to this project was not accounted for when Covington was approved for development. He suggested that eliminating the curb cut on Bessemer Road would not accomplish diverting traffic; having both the access on Bessemer and through Covington would be preferred. Planning Commission

Ms. Sarah Hamblin, Seamon, Whiteside, and Associates, reviewed the request with the Commission.

Mr. Chapman suggested that the mail kiosk should be relocated to prevent a traffic hazard at the ingress/egress. Ms. Hamblin answered that this could be reviewed.

Mr. Neal thanked the applicant for the addition of the sidewalk. He asked the reason for removal of tree #30. Ms. Hamblin answered that it is in poor condition and in a drainage easement. Mr. Neal asked about tree #32. Ms. Hamblin answered that it is in poor condition and would be affected by drainage. Mr. Neal asked if the tree was located in the buffer. Ms. Hamblin answered in the affirmative. Mr. Neal suggested that it should be preserved. Ms. Hamblin answered that this could be considered. Mr. Neal asked about tree #18. Ms. Hamblin answered that it is in a utility easement. Mr. Neal suggested that this could be preserved as well. Mr. Kevin Steelman answered that #32 could be preserved with restudy of tree #30.

Mr. McNeill asked how the trees would be mitigated given the significant number of mitigation inches required. Mr. Steelman answered that there is adjacent HOA property where a significant number of trees could be planted. Mr. McNeill expressed concern with the typical “clear cutting of property” for development and suggested that as many trees should be preserved as possible. Mr. Steelman agreed and stated that there are increased drainage requirements from the state that requires more and more grading to be accomplished which further impacts development and preservation of trees. He stated that this in turn causes more clear cutting of property.

Mr. Steelman stated that they would like to tie into the sidewalk already approved and planned for the adjacent development in order to not duplicate sidewalks on Bessemer Road.

Mr. Chapman suggested that the sidewalk should be extended to the other side of the pond. Mr. Steelman answered that this could be accomplished and would provide a destination to the pond. He suggested that a crossover could then be provided to connect to the sidewalk on the other side of Bessemer Road. Planning Commission

Ms. Gregg asked if a pathway could be provided for the remaining portion of the property where the HOA property and tree mitigation is proposed. Mr. Steelman answered that there are buffers between properties, so a path might not be possible. Ms. Gregg asked how some of the mitigation would be achieved. Mr. Steelman answered that some of the trees within the buffers could count toward the mitigation required. Mr. Bernard clarified how the tree mitigation is determined and that the mitigation required is based only on the project acreage.

Ms. Campaigne expressed concern with not extending the sidewalk along Bessemer Road. She suggested that the amount of traffic could be a pedestrian safety issue. Mr. Steelman answered that this could be considered and potentially completed by the HOA. Ms. Campaigne suggested that a pervious pathway or bike path should be considered. Mr. Steelman answered that this could be considered.

Ms. Smith expressed concern with not having traditional sidewalks. She suggested that the sidewalk should be required to connect to Larch Lane.

Mr. Neal moved for approval of the request including all staff comments, excluding staff’s comment to extend the sidewalk to the lake with following conditions:  Save trees #30 and #32;  move kiosk deeper into the subdivision and coordinate with staff on an appropriate location;  sidewalk should connect from Covington to the lake as suggested by applicant. Mr. Chapman seconded the motion.

Mr. Neal stated that he would rather have a natural path for the remaining area from the lake to Larch Lane given the topography of the area. He suggested that an asphalt or gravel pathway would not be appropriate.

Mr. McNeill moved to amend the motion to add a crosswalk from the end of the proposed sidewalk to connect with the sidewalk on the other side of Bessemer Road. Mr. Neal seconded the motion. Planning Commission

Mr. Mitchell stated that the Transportation Department approves the location of crosswalks and stated that given the location of the intersection, a crosswalk would likely not be approved at this location.

Mr. McNeill withdrew his amendment. Mr. Neal withdrew his second.

Ms. Campaigne suggested that the applicant leverage their influence to request the extension and improvements for a sidewalk from the proposed sidewalk to Larch Lane. Mr. Mitchell clarified that the sidewalk would be in the right-of- way.

Ms. Campaigne moved to amend the motion to direct the applicant discuss with the HOA the option of applying for an encroachment permit and funding the additional sidewalk portion as suggested by Mr. Steelman.

Mr. Pagliarini stated that the Commission cannot condition the approval based on the action of a third party. Ms. Campaigne withdrew her motion.

Ms. Smith expressed concern with the project, the removal of trees and tree mitigation that would be required. She stated that based on this, she would not be supporting this project.

Ms. Gregg asked for clarification on what purview the Commission would have regarding the sidewalks. Mr. Chapman answered that during the recent changes to the Dunes West/Park West PDs, a portion of this property was deeded to the HOA. He stated that the Commission cannot bind the HOA as a third party entity to complete the sidewalks as the HOA is not the applicant.

Mr. McNeill suggested that Mr. Steelman has controlling interest of the HOA. Mr. Pagliarini answered that the HOA is a separate entity and cannot be subjected to conditions regarding this request.

Mr. Millet moved to convene into executive session for legal advice. Ms. Smith seconded the motion. All in favor. Planning Commission

The Commission convened into executive session at 6:26 pm and reconvened at 6:30 pm. No decisions made during executive session.

Mr. Chapman called for a vote on the motion. Motion passed on a 6 to 2 vote with Ms. Campaigne, Mr. Chapman, Mr. McNeill, Mr. Millet, Mr. Neal, and Mr. Cuttino in favor; Ms. Gregg and Ms. Smith opposed.

label: 84 Belle Point Drive
request: Request to rezone from AB, Areawide Business District, to AB-2, Areawide Business-2 District, located at 84 Belle Point Drive. TMS No.: 556-00-00-294

events.text:
Ms. Canon reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2).

Ms. Smith asked the reason for the zoning change. Ms. Canon answered that a boat storage use was desired so AB-2 would be required along with a Special Exception through the Board of Zoning Appeals. She stated that there was also interest in using the property for bus storage for Charleston County School District (CCSD).

Mr. Millet asked if this was previously requested. Ms. Canon answered that the last request was in 2014; Town Council denied the request.

Mr. David Bunch reviewed the request with the Commission. He stated that they originally annexed into the Town to receive water and sewer service. He stated that the zoning request is to use the property for camper and boat storage. He stated that he has also been approached by CCSD for school bus storage on the site as well.

Mr. Wren asked if the discussion with CCSD was to move the bus storage from the old Wando High School site to this property. Mr. Bunch answered in the affirmative and stated that he has only had some initial inquiries. He stated that he is limited in how the property can be used because he cannot get access to water and sewer. Planning Commission

Mr. Neal asked about the property taxes. Mr. Bunch answered that the property taxes would be over $19,000 per year.

Mr. Millet asked about water and sewer service. Mr. Bunch answered that in order to get water and sewer it would have to be connected from Paul Foster Road, which because of the distance would be very cost prohibitive and would entail crossing multiple properties.

Mr. Mark Nelson, 343 Bridgetown Pass, stated that the property is currently zoned AB. He expressed concern that rezoning to AB2 would allow more intensive uses and expressed concern with the potential for increased traffic. He expressed concern that the property would be utilized for truck or bus storage and that this is a more high volume traffic use.

Ms. Lisa Schnipke, 185 Mossy Oak Way, expressed concern the rezoning request would increase traffic. She expressed concern with having bus storage on the property. She also expressed concern that if approved, other uses not consistent with the character of the neighborhood would be allowed.

Mr. Bunch noted that he is no longer associated with a trucking company and does not intend to have any truck storage on the property. He stated that the intention is to only have boat and camper storage.

Mr. Neal asked if Mr. Bunch would be amenable to a deferral in order to have a site plan showing the potential layout. Mr. Bunch answered that his understanding was that this was the first step in the process.

Mr. Chapman closed the public hearing.

Mr. Neal asked if the request can be conditioned. Ms. Canon answered in the negative and stated that a special exception would be required from BOZA and if approved, would be tied to a specific site plan. Mr. Neal asked if the rezoning was approved but the special exception denied. Ms. Canon answered if the special exception for outdoor storage was not approved, but the rezoning request was approved, then all AB-2 uses would be allowed. Planning Commission

Ms. Campaigne asked if outdoor storage is allowed in AB. Ms. Canon answered in the negative.

Mr. Millet moved for denial of the rezoning request. Mr. Neal seconded the motion.

Ms. Smith suggested that it is important to review requests based on what is appropriate for the property and the surrounding neighborhood. She suggested that the proper zoning for the property is AB, not AB-2.

Mr. Neal agreed with Ms. Smith and stated that the property rights of the surrounding property owners should be taken into consideration as well.

Mr. Chapman called for a vote on the motion. All in favor.

Ms. Farrell reviewed the request with the Committee (attachment 1). She stated that the Planning Commission recommended denial.

Mr. Carrier asked about the AB-2 zoning and if the special exception would require Board of Zoning Appeals (BOZA) approval. Ms. Farrell answered in the affirmative and stated that the commercial development would require DRB approval as well. Mr. Carrier asked for clarification on the Planning Commission discussion on this issue. Ms. Farrell answered that the property owner has been unable to obtain sewer service to the site; but that should sewer be provided, Planning Committee

then he indicated that he would be comfortable with the existing zoning. She stated that while the owner has indicated that the use would only be for boat and camper storage, the zoning would provide other uses such as a gas station. She stated that most of the uses allowed under AB-2 are also allowed in AB. She stated that some other uses such as outdoor storage would be allowed under AB-2 with special exception approval from BOZA. She stated that the Charleston Council School District (CCSD) did approach the owner regarding utilizing the property for school bus storage, which could be done if the zoning were approved and a special exception approved.

Mr. Smith asked if there were any concerns with bus storage versus camper and boat storage. Ms. Farrell answered that she is not sure, but the owner indicated that he would not provide the school bus storage if there was opposition for such on the property.

Mr. Bustos moved to recommend to Town Council denial of the request. Motion fails due to the lack of a second.

Mr. Carrier moved to recommend to Town Council approval of the request. Mr. Smith seconded the motion.

Mr. Smith stated that the property owner has been before the Planning Commission on several occasions trying to find uses for development of the property. He stated that the lack of access for water and sewer has been challenging for the owner. He asked if staff has any recommendations that might work for the owner, Town Council, and the public. Mr. DeMoura answered that a unified development plan for the properties in that area would have been the best option in regard to uses, traffic, etc.

Mr. Carrier suggested that with the approval of a Chick Fil-A on the adjacent corner, the amount of traffic in that area would be increased. He suggested that uses that would not significantly increase traffic would be the best option.

Mr. Brimmer expressed concern that approval of the request would allow uses that would be of a more intense use and suggested that this was not the best option. Planning Committee

Mr. Smith asked if a special exception could be allowed under the current zoning. Ms. Farrell answered in the negative. Mr. DeMoura suggested that there appears to be some obstacle with being able to provide water and sewer for the property and suggested that it might be tied to monetary reasons.

Mr. Bustos suggested that an appropriate use within the existing zoning should be considered.

Mr. Brimmer called for a vote on the motion. Motion failed on a 1 to 3 vote with Mr. Carrier in favor; Mr. Smith, Mr. Brimmer, and Mr. Bustos opposed.

label: Venning Road / Rifle Range Road
request: Request approval of Waiver from Land Development Regulations Section 155.047, and approval of Sketch Plan for two lots on the corner of Venning Road and Rifle Range Road, located at Venning Road / Rifle Range Road. TMS No.: 560-00-00-012

events.text:
Ms. Canon reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2).

Ms. Smith asked if the neighbors are aware of the request and satisfied. Ms. Canon answered that she is not sure, but the property was properly posted and advertised. She stated that no correspondence was received. Planning Commission

Mr. Millet asked if a structure would be placed on the property. Ms. Canon answered that she is not sure and suggested that the applicant could better address the question.

Mr. Neal suggested that the land waiver should be considered in conjunction with this request. Mr. Chapman agreed.

Mr. Mitchell reviewed staff comments related to the waiver with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2).

Mr. Neal asked about the sliver portion of the property. Mr. Mitchell answered that is a portion of the property that is within the Seaside Farms Planned Development. Mr. Neal asked the reason for the waiver. Mr. Mitchell answered that the waiver is needed in order to allow the subdivision.

Ms. Jenny Germuth, Seamon, Whiteside, and Associates, reviewed the request with the Commission.

Mr. Chapman suggested that this is a good, proactive plan from MPW.

There being no comments, Mr. Chapman closed the public hearing.

Ms. Germuth noted that the waiver would be temporary and only be in place so that the properties could be aggregated.

Ms. Smith moved for approval of the rezoning request for item 5C, including all staff comments. Mr. Neal seconded the motion. All in favor.

Mr. Neal moved for approval of the sketch plan and LDR waiver for item 5D, including all staff comments. Mr. Wren seconded the motion. All in favor.

label: Six Mile Road / John Ballam Road
request: Request to annex and zone PD-CD, Planned Development-Conservation Design District, four parcels of land, for a proposed development to be known as The Farm at Oyster Point, located at Six Mile Road / John Ballam Road. TMS Nos.: 561-00-00-055; -058; -059; -067

events.text:
Ms. Canon reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2).

Mr. Neal asked if John Ballam Road is a private road. Ms. Canon answered that the recorded plat shows John Ballam as a dedicated public roadway.

Mr. Pagliarini stated that he received correspondence from Mr. John Haggerty, attorney, indicating that John Ballam is a private road. He stated that he reviewed the recorded plat which included property signatures and noted the public dedication of the roadway. He stated that in addition, the roadway is publicly maintained. He stated that it is the Town’s position that John Ballam Road is a public roadway. Planning Commission

Mr. Wofford Stribling, Earthsource Engineering, reviewed the request with the Commission.

Mr. Chapman asked about lot size and why the reduction of the lot sizes from 12,500 to 6,000. Mr. Stribling answered that the smaller lot sizes were proposed to provide more open space and an open space perimeter around the project.

Mr. Neal asked about the barn area and if it was added to the project. Mr. Stribling answered that it was always included with the project. Mr. Neal suggested that the layout is not consistent with a conservation design. Mr. Stribling answered that there was an effort to provide multiple interconnectivity points.

Mr. Louis Jefferson, 1128 McKnight Road and on CAGE Board, stated that they support the surrounding resident’s opinion regarding this project. He expressed concern with the traffic impact to the surrounding neighborhood.

Mr. Bernard King, 2175 Kweteng Drive, stated that he is opposed to this project because of the traffic impact. He suggested that the project is not consistent with the surrounding neighborhood.

Ms. Jefferson stated that she disagrees that John Ballam Road is a public road. She stated that her research shows that the road is private. She stated that the road is not publicly maintained. She suggested that improvements were made when the roadway was damaged during maintenance of an easement. She stated that she is opposed to project and suggested that the project is not consistent with the character of the neighborhood.

Ms. Pat Sullivan, 1002 Plantation Court, suggested that the character of an established neighborhood should be maintained. She suggested that more attention to cultural landscape design and cluster development should be given for this project.

Mr. George Freeman, 1450 Bowman Road, suggested that there should be interconnectivity. He suggested that this project would increase traffic on Rifle Range Road. He suggested that having 12,500 sf lots would be more consistent with the surrounding neighborhood. Planning Commission

Ms. Gloria Walker, 2155 Rifle Range Road, expressed concerned with the number of lots proposed and that the project is not consistent with the surrounding neighborhood. She expressed concern that the project would increase traffic in the area. She expressed concern that trails would not be open to the public. She suggested that the concerns of the existing residents should be taken into serious consideration.

Mr. Stribling stated that the restriction of ADUs within the project was proposed to help alleviate traffic impacts. He stated that they have made an effort to save as many trees on the lots as possible. He stated that even though the lots are smaller, the density of three lots to the acre has been maintained. He suggested that this is the best use of the property.

Mr. Neal moved for denial of the request. Ms. Campaigne seconded the motion.

Ms. Campaigne stated that there are a number of concerns that need to be addressed. She suggested that this is not an appropriate project for the area.

Ms. Smith agreed and suggested that the project does not meet any of the criteria for PD-CD. She suggested that property should not always be developed to the maximum allowed.

Mr. Neal agreed that the project is not appropriate for the neighborhood.

Mr. Millet suggested that there should be preservation of established communities and the culture and character of the established neighborhoods should be maintained.

Mr. Chapman called for a vote on the motion. All in favor.

the Charleston County RMC Office in Plat Book BV, Page 082; and (iv) an approximately 1.00 acre parcel located at 2265 John Ballam Road, identified by TMS No. 561-00-00-067, and depicted on a plat recorded by the Charleston County RMC Office in Plat Book BV, Page 082. Planning Committee

Ms. Farrell reviewed the request with the Committee (attachment 1). She stated that the Planning Commission recommended denial of the zoning request.

Mr. Bustos asked the location of the project. Ms. Farrell showed the location on the map for the Committee.

Mr. Smith asked about the goals of a PD-CD and how this project does or does not meet the intent. Ms. Farrell answered that the confederate line is located to the right of the project and has over the 25% amount of open space required. Mr. Smith asked if there are ADUs. Ms. Farrell answered in the negative and stated that the applicant has indicated that ADUs would not be allowed. Mr. Smith asked if the project could be developed in the county. Ms. Farrell answered that they would need to have approval for a PD because of the lot size requirement. Mr. Smith asked what open space would be required in the county. Ms. Farrell answered that she was not sure, but it would be less than 25%.

Mr. Carrier asked if staff met with the applicant prior to submittal of the request. Ms. Farrell answered in the affirmative, both verbally and through written comments.

Mr. Bustos asked if ADUs are being proposed. Ms. Farrell answered that the applicant has indicated no ADUs would not be allowed. Mr. Bustos asked the reason for the project not being more in keeping with the PD-CD. Ms. Farrell suggested that the applicant could better address this.

Mr. Brimmer suggested that the plan does not meet the intent of the PD-CD and is designed more as a traditional neighborhood.

Mr. Wofford Stribling, Earthsource Engineering, reviewed the project with the Committee. He showed a traditional layout for the site for the Committee and suggested that the proposed layout meets the intent of the PD-CD with the clustering of the open space, inclusion of an extensive trail system, smaller lots, and inclusion of farming and barns. Planning Committee

Mr. Smith asked for clarification of the open space near the pond. Mr. Stribling answered that they are proposing a dock and picnic area on the pond.

Mr. Brimmer asked the reason for not restricting ADUs for the traditional layout. Mr. Stribling answered that the traditional layout was to show what would be allowed compared to what is proposed.

Mr. Bustos asked if the traditional layout would be allowed. Ms. Farrell answered that she is not sure as some calculations would be necessary to ensure compliance with open space requirements, lot sizes, etc.

Mr. Henry Ballam expressed concern with the amount of traffic already on Six Mile Road and that this would increase the traffic.

Ms. Claudia Mazyck, 1285 Six Mile Road, distributed a copy of a GIS map showing the lot sizes of the surrounding properties. She suggested that this project would not be in keeping with the character of the community.

Ms. Sullivan distributed photos for the Committee to review. She stated that as indicated in the photos, the homes are smaller and on larger lots than what would be developed with the requested project. She suggested that the project is not in keeping with the Comprehensive Plan and not in keeping with the community. She suggested that the proposed project would increase property taxes for the surrounding properties. She suggested that the project would not be positive for the community and suggested that the request should be denied.

Ms. Gloria Walker, 2155 Rifle Range Road, suggested that the project is not in keeping with the neighborhood and should not be approved.

Mr. George Freeman, 1450 Bowman Road, stated that interconnectivity should be included in the project to provide relief from additional traffic on Rifle Range Road. He suggested that the recommended Community Conservation (CC) zoning should be upheld as this would keep the recommended density of three units per acre intact as well as require 12,500 sf lots. He stated that ADUs are not allowed by right, and should not be allowed as it would increase the density.

Mr. Lewis Jefferson, 1128 McKnight Road, agrees with the previous comments. He expressed concern with not being able to hear the proceedings and Planning Committee

suggested that better audio should considered. Mr. Brimmer stated that this should hopefully be alleviated with the new Town Hall building.

Mr. Carey Mathison, developer, stated that they would be amenable to changing the name of the project. He stated that from a marketing standpoint, this project does fit within the community. He stated that they have included interconnectivity in the event this is able to be accommodated in the future.

Mr. Smith asked if the size of the homes is known. Ms. Farrell answered in the negative. Mr. Smith asked if the traditional layout is accurate in terms of the number of lots. Ms. Farrell answered that she is not sure.

Mr. Carrier moved to recommend to Town Council denial of the annexation and zoning request. Motion failed due to the lack of a second.

Mr. Smith moved for to recommend to Town Council approval of the annexation request. Mr. Bustos seconded the motion. All in favor.

Mr. Smith moved to recommend to Town Council for approval of the zoning request. Motion failed due to the lack of a second.

Mr. Bustos suggested that the developer should work with staff in regard to the design of the project.

Mr. Brimmer moved to recommend to Town Council denial of the zoning request. Mr. Carrier seconded the motion. Motion passed on a 3 to 1 vote with Mr. Brimmer, Mr. Carrier, and Mr. Bustos in favor; Mr. Smith opposed.

The Committee convened for a short break at 2:50 pm and reconvened at 2:56 pm.

George Freeman, 1450 Bowman Road, stated that he is just hearing about this deferral and feels that it is a great injustice to the citizens of Six Mile. He stated that they have been fighting this issue for quite some time and vented their concerns at the Planning Commission and the Planning Committee meetings. He stated that this project is not something that should go into the Six Mile Community. He stated that it should not be deferred, but disapproved, and come back again when the Town has a better comprehensive plan in place. He stated that this project is not something that is desired for the Six Mile Community and only adds more traffic and does not have inter-connectivity and totally against the lot size that was requested in the comprehensive plan. He pleaded with Council not to defer, but to deny this project. Mr. Carrier asked if the applicant has a right to request for a deferral and be granted one. Mr. Pagliarini stated that this is Council’s discretion. Bernard King, 2175 Kweteng Drive, stated that this will have a negative impact on the community and said that he is opposing this project. He stated that the community does not need, they do not want it and it is not in conjunction with the comprehensive plan. He is in hopes that Town Council will deny this project.

Lewis Jefferson, 1128 McKnight Road, stated that Mr. Freeman said it well. He said that it would be a great offensive to the Six Mile Community to have this issue deferred. He stated that this is a disruption and they are looking at the project as an additional 23 homes to Oyster Point, which is a monster in itself in terms of the intersection of Rifle Range Road and Six Mile. He stated that it is a right in, right out for these 23 homes and there is potential for there to be more than 23 homes if approved at 6,000 sf per lot as opposed to the required 12,500 sf per lot. He stated that there are a number of reasons for Council to base their refusal of this project. He stated that he and others have spent a great deal of time with the Planning Commission and Planning Committee and they have successfully rejected this project based on the rules at hand and they are asking Council to do the same this evening. Pat Sullivan, 1002 Plantation Court, stated that she is going to ask Council not to defer and vote to deny this request tonight. She stated that this development does not do this. She said that the developer advised that this is a creative plan. She said that it is a cul-de-sac with one way in and one way out. She said they are all over Mount Pleasant and the Town does not need this in this community. She said that the pictures she is distributing at this time are photographs that she took on John Ballam Road and said that the houses are in no way close to what these developers want to put in. She said that they are small homes on a large piece of property with lots of t

to amend the Urban Corridor Overlay District. He would like to first thank the Planning Committee for its unanimous support. He said the proposal to remove Ben Sawyer from Rifle Range to the Ben Sawyer Bridge does not; however, create a distinct district for that portion of Ben Sawyer which is the gateway and entrance into Mount Pleasant from the islands. As such, this special district should have commensurate zoning to reflect its unique status and significance to the Town. To recommend revalidations and modification to this zoning which should be done expeditiously to avoid any possibility of further monstrosities that are out of character for what is intended for this area such as Sullivan’s Point and whatever is to be built on the Atlantic property. He would also like to request that any impact assessments, especially as it pertains to traffic, be scrutinized very closely since, in his opinion, the Town has not been served well in this regard on the path regarding Ben Sawyer. George Freeman, 1450 Bowman Road, read the following statement: At the Transportation Committee, the committee reviewed three transportation options for the Rifle Range Road Park. The Community Action Group for Encouragement (CAGE), has a fourth option. Extend the road from the roundabout on Rifle Range Road to the main road in the park. solves the problem that was mentioned in the Transportation Committee and hopes that the Town will work with them to make this a reality. MaryAnne Taylor, 427 Greenbriar Lane, Charleston, stated that her comments are more of a public services announcement, as well as to extend an invitation to Mayor, Council and those in attendance. She is a member of the East Cooper Republican Women’s Club and they have a fundraiser every year. She said it is held at Alhambra Hall where they also choose to buy and serve local shrimp, because they believe in supporting the local vendors. She said the shrimp will come from Mount Pleasant Shrimp Company. She said the event will be held September 13th from 5:30 to 7:30 pm, and she would love for Mayor and Council, as well as their family and friends to purchase a ticket and attend. She said they will have keynote speakers at this event; however, the important aspect is that they give their money back to the community. She said they support fellow republicans who are running which is one of their objectives. However, they also support the Low Country Orphan Relief, as well as Veterans in the military and support the Lowcountry tri-county Veterans Group. She said their funding does not simply support political activities, but also goes back into the community as well.

request: Request approval of Sketch Plan for Carolina Park Phase 12A and 12B, 83 single-family lots, zoned PD, Planned Development District, located off Carolina Park Boulevard. TMS No.: 598-03-00-863

events.text:
Mr. Bernard reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2).

Ms. Niermann reviewed the project with the Commission. She stated that they are amenable to working with staff on all aspects.

Mr. Chapman asked if this project would be clear cut. Ms. Niermann answered that tree protection would be installed to preserve trees to be retained. Mr. Chapman asked if the tree protection is inspected. Ms. Niermann answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Wren asked if this project is in a flood zone. Ms. Niermann answered in the affirmative. Mr. Wren asked if the fill is needed to bring the property out of the flood zone. Ms. Niermann answered in the negative and stated that the fill is Planning Commission

needed to have the lots at the same grade or near the same grade as the roadway.

Mr. Millet asked about lot 47 and why the tree is scheduled for removal. Ms. Niermann answered there is a utility easement on the property and if the tree were not removed, the lot would be unbuildable.

label: Highway 17N Between Theodore Road
request: Request approval of Preliminary Plat for Bees Crossing (FKA Beehive Tract), 90 single-family lots zoned R-4, Medium Density Residential District, located at Highway 17N Between Theodore Road and Beehive Road. TMS No.: 614-00-00-108; -109; -110; -124; and -607

events.text:
Ms. Salomon reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2). She stated that comment #3 was an oversight by staff and comment #7 is not required as this preliminary plat falls under the previous plat submittal requirements.

Mr. Neal asked about comment #4. Ms. Salomon indicated the location on the site plan for the Commission.

Mr. Bernard clarified tree removal comments. Planning Commission

Mr. Chapman asked if some of the trees could be preserved. Mr. Bernard answered that the removal was possibly due to grading issues and suggested that the applicant could better address this issue.

label: 1750 Palmetto Isle Drive
request: Request to amend the River Island Plantation, Planned Development (PD) District, ordinance providing for the construction, operation and maintenance of a stealth wireless communications facility including a tower not to exceed 140 feet, located at 1750 Palmetto Isle Drive. TMS # 540-00-00-066

events.text:
Ms. Canon reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2).

Ms. Smith asked about the design of the tower. Ms. Canon answered in the negative and suggested that the applicant might be able to better address.

Mr. Jonathan Yates reviewed the request with the Commission (attachment 3).

Mr. Robert Hill, representative for T-mobile, explained the need for the cell tower. He showed a depiction of the locations of the current cell towers located near Rivertowne and the coverage for the area (attachment 3). He stated that they had several community meetings regarding this request.

Mr. Wren asked if there are existing locations where the tower could be located and if the clubhouse could be utilized. Mr. Hill answered that the height of the Planning Commission

building would not allow the coverage needed. Mr. Wren asked if the tower would only service Rivertowne. Mr. Hill answered that based on the height and the amount of foliage, the tower would provide service for approximately ½ mile to 1 mile from the tower.

Mr. Millet asked the proximity of residential to the proposed location. Mr. Hill showed the location of the residential and proximity on the map for the Commission. Mr. Millet asked about the coverage. Mr. Keith Powell, representative for Verizon, showed the proposed coverage to the Commission.

Mr. Yates stated that the tower would serve several different wireless communication companies. He stated that the tower would be a stealth pole with an equipment building.

Mr. Michael Robinson, Charleston Appraisal, stated that he conducted an analysis on the effects of the construction of a cell tower in Mount Pleasant to property values and provided this information for the Commission to review (attachment 4). He stated that based on his analysis there was no impact to property values.

Mr. Powell reviewed how the tower would be seen from different areas near the proposed location for the Commission.

Mr. Yates stated that they conducted a community survey and Mr. Will Freeland reviewed the findings with the Commission. Mr. Freeland stated that approximately 79% of those that responded to the survey were in favor of the proposed tower.

Mr. Hank Cardarelli, 1864 Great Hope Drive, expressed concern that the cell tower would negatively affect property values. He stated that the HOA has covenants and restrictions regarding cell towers.

Mr. Robert Newman, 1836 Delacourt Ave, stated that they currently have low coverage and is in favor of the tower.

Mr. Kent Provada, Palmetto Isle, suggested that the survey should not be considered as it did not include an opportunity to consider other locations or Planning Commission

alternatives. He suggested that the cell tower could be placed on other property along Highway 41 that would provide coverage.

Mr. Michael Baumrind, 1537 Red Drum Road, stated that he supports the proposal. He stated that he works from home and finds that cell service is low in the area. He stated that he supports the request to provide better coverage. He suggested that the younger generation highly considers cell coverage when considering purchasing a home. He suggested that the additional tower would better distribute the volume, which would provide better service for the entire area.

Ms. Nina Thomas, 1824 Palmetto Isle Drive, expressed concern for the potential radiation that the cell tower could emit and that it would cause health issues for children and residents in the surrounding area. She suggested that the tower is too close in proximity to residential neighborhoods and amenities. She suggested that the proposal is unacceptable and should not be approved.

Mr. Jeff Poplar, president of HOA of Pointe in North Creek and on the board of Parker’s Island HOA. He stated that wireless capability within neighborhoods is a necessity for home sales. He suggested that a majority of homes do not have landline phones and rely solely on cell service.

Ms. Kelly Wood, 1872 Great Hope Drive, stated that she is opposed to the request and agrees with the concerns of Ms. Thomas. She suggested that the proximity of the cell tower could increase the chances of cancer.

Mr. Joe Daily, member of Parkers Landing and Parkers Island boards, stated that the boards are in favor of the request. He stated that many homes no longer have land lines and rely on cell phones as their main telephone access. He suggested that not having good wireless service and coverage is also a safety issue as residents would possibly not be able to reach emergency personnel during emergency events. He asked that the request be approved.

Ms. Pam Fischette, 2528 Ballast Point, agrees that the proximity of the cell tower would increase the amount of radiation in the area. She suggested that other locations should be considered that would not be so close to residents. Planning Commission

Ms. Linda Woodfern, 1837 Palmetto Isle Drive, agreed that there is a safety issue with the location of the towers and agrees with Ms. Thomas’ comments. She agreed that a different location should be considered. She suggested that a booster can be provided from the different wireless carriers and suggested that this could be an alternative to constructing a new tower. She stated that she is opposed to the proposed location of the tower.

Ms. Sharon Salomon, 1844 Great Hope, stated that she is opposed to the location of the tower. She stated that there are a number of health concerns related to cell towers and radiation. She suggested that a different location should be considered.

Mr. Paul Cessna, 2791 Olympia Fields Lane, stated that as a chemical engineer, he is not aware of the type of radiation that a cell tower gives off causing health concerns. He stated that the radiation emitted is less energy than visible light. He stated that he is in favor of the request and suggested that the additional tower is needed to provide needed wireless service for the surrounding area. He suggested that the it is proposed in an appropriate location. He asked that the request be approved.

Ms. Susan Matthews, member of Parkers Landing POA, expressed concern with health issues and child safety, but does not see that this would be a health issue or that the request would affect property values. She asked that the request be approved.

Mr. Daniel Gingrich, 1621 Oak Crest Drive, expressed concern that the boosters previously mentioned have a short range. He stated that he has trouble with service in his home. He suggested that if aesthetics is a concern, there are different designs such as towers that look like trees that can be considered. He asked that the request be approved.

Mr. Hill stated that the penetration rate of radio frequency is minimal and there has been no evidence that it causes health issues. He stated that they did look at different locations, but the proposed location was considered the best option to provide the best service for the area. He stated that the different designs were also considered, but the stealth tower is considered the best option and would provide service to a greater area. Planning Commission

Ms. Campaigne closed the public hearing.

Mr. Cuttino asked the required distance the tower must be from residential uses. Ms. Canon answered that the distance from residential must be equal to the height of the tower.

Mr. Millet asked what consideration the Board has. Ms. Canon answered that the request is a PD amendment so the Commission has the option to either approve the request, approve with conditions, or deny the request. She stated that if approved, it would be a permitted use allowed within the PD.

Mr. Wren moved for approval of the request. Ms. Campaigne seconded the motion.

Mr. Wren agreed that the wireless service is very poor in the area. He stated that as a father with small children, he is concerned with health and safety, but has not seen any correlation of cell towers causing health issues.

Ms. Smith agreed that there has not been evidence that the cell towers cause health issues. She stated that wireless service is now a vital part of life.

Mr. McNeill suggested that there are not sufficient reasons to deny the request.

Ms. Campaigne stated that she is concerned with health and safety issues as well, but suggested that there is not sufficient evidence that cell towers cause health issues.

Mr. Cuttino suggested that the need for cell service in the area outweighs any minor radiation concerns.

Ms. Campaigne called for a vote on the motion. All in favor with Mr. Chapman abstaining.

The Board convened at 6:24 pm for a short break and reconvened at 6:26 pm. Planning Commission

Ms. Farrell reviewed the request with the Committee (attachment 1). She stated that the Commission recommended approval of the request.

Mr. Brimmer stated that due to time constraints a detailed review from the applicant would not be possible, but noted that the Committee received the presentation from the applicant ahead of time.

Mr. Jonathan Yates, attorney for the applicant reviewed the request with the Committee.

Mr. Robert Hill, representative for T-Mobile, stated that this request would enhance and provide additional coverage for the area of Rivertowne.

Mr. Michael Robinson, Charleston Appraisal, state that they conducted an appraisal of the surrounding area and found that there were no changes with the property values after a cell tower was constructed.

Mr. Will Freeland, Moody O’Neill CPA, stated that they conducted a survey of the Rivertowne residents regarding the request. He stated that of the 708 surveys sent out, they received approximately 354 valid responses or a 50.5% response rate. He stated that approximately 281 were in favor or 79.4% and 73 were opposed or 20.6%.

Mr. Ken Favata, 1852 Great Hope Drive, suggested that the impacts of cell towers should be minimized. He referenced section 156.113 that states that cell towers should be deployed “while preserving the intrinsic aesthetic character of the community”. He suggested that other locations that would be Planning Committee

more appropriate should be considered first. He suggested that cell towers should not be an allowed use.

Mr. Hank Caradelli, 1864 Great Hope Drive, read a portion of the survey that was sent to the Rivertowne residents and suggested that it discounts the survey. He suggested that it was not determined whether the homes studied were in proximity of the proposed tower.

Ms. Sharon Salamone, 1844 Great Hope Drive, suggested that not all of the residents on Great Hope Drive received the survey. She suggested that those most affected by the request were not surveyed. She suggested that the cell tower would affect property values.

Ms. Patricia Felenczak, 1825 Great Hope Drive, suggested that Palmetto Isle is a small portion of the Rivertowne Community. She stated that she is opposed to the request.

Ms. Susan Matthews, Parker Island POA member, suggested that lack of cell coverage would negatively affect property values. She suggested that it is a safety issue as well as the ability to dial 911 is diminished. She suggested that having the cell tower would be a benefit.

Mr. Bill Daily, Parker Island POA member, stated that he is in favor of the request. He suggested that approximately 82% of residents have a cell phone, and approximately 50% of homes have cell phone service as their main phone service.

Mr. Fran Licausi, Parkers Landing, expressed concern with being able to reach emergency services. He suggested that better cell service is needed.

Mr. Paul Comer, 2721 Sarazen, stated that better cell phone service is needed.

Mr. Jacob Curtis, 1805 Great Hope, stated that he is not in favor of the request.

Ms. Nancy Tyler, 1865 Great Hope Drive, stated that she is not in favor of the location of the cell tower. She suggested that a different location should be considered that is not in proximity to residents. Planning Committee

Ms. Susan Grady, 2727 Parkers Landing, stated that she is in favor of the request as well as the majority of the residents within the Parkers Landing POA. She suggested that it is necessary to have strong, steady, reliable cell service for emergency reasons and safety.

Mr. Cunnane, suggested that there is not sufficient fire protection services. He suggested that the services needed for additional residential neighborhoods should be considered before the neighborhoods are approved.

Mr. Ben Salamone, 1844 Great Hope, agreed that the location of the cell tower should be reconsidered. He questioned why other locations were not considered. He suggested that a different location would not affect the residential homes or the property values.

Mr. Paul Cessa, 2791 Olympia Fields Lane, stated that everyone wants sufficient service, home property values that are not affected, and receive the services that are needed. He suggested that there is not definitive information that a cell tower would affect property values. He stated that inadequate cell phone service would definitively affect the property values and has a domino effect with surrounding properties. He stated that the applicant has adequately addressed that the location proposed is the best location to provide the needed area coverage. He suggested that this request should be approved.

Mr. Patrick Faver, 1869 Great Hope Drive, suggested that the issue is not whether additional cell phone coverage is needed, but where the tower would be located. He suggested that there has not been evidence that this location is the best and that other locations were considered.

Mr. Carrier asked if other locations were considered. Mr. Robert Hill, T-Mobile, answered in the affirmative and stated that they have several co-locations in the area. He stated that the Harris Teeter, the water tower, SCE&G transmission towers, etc. were all considered, but the locations were not viable, or they were not able to negotiate the co-location. Mr. Carrier asked about the assessment of the other neighborhoods and where the towers were located. Mr. Hill answered that one of the towers is behind a restaurant on Hwy 41 at Charleston National; the tower at Dunes West is behind the Fire Station. Mr. Carrier asked the height of the towers. Mr. Hill answered that the Charleston national tower is approximately 140 feet and the other is approximately 150 feet. Planning Committee

Mr. Smith asked the setback requirements for cell towers. Ms. Farrell answered that the request is to amend the PD for this to be a permitted use. She stated that the closest residential property line is approximately 104 feet. She stated that as a special exception, the cell tower would have to be the same distance from the residence as the height of the tower.

Mr. Carrier asked the difference in this request from other requests such as the cell tower near Candlewood. Ms. Farrell answered that the regulations in place today differ from the regulations in place when the Candlewood cell tower was approved. She stated that the current regulations were enacted as a result of the concerns with the cell tower near Candlewood.

Mr. Bustos asked about cell coverage. Mr. Cessa answered that if he cannot get good cell service, he uses his landline. He stated that his neighbor frequently travels to a location where he can get sufficient cell service.

Mr. Brimmer asked about consideration of different locations for the cell tower. Mr. Yates answered that there is seldom a location where there is not some opposition. He stated that they typically look for locations that will provide the best and largest coverage area that are in commercial areas or other appropriate locations. He stated that the proposed area would be located near the golf course maintenance area. He stated that the tower would be visible as this is necessary to get sufficient coverage. Mr. Brimmer asked if there is a report on what other locations were considered. Mr. Keith Powell, Optima Towers, answered that they did consider other locations. He stated that the requested location was considered the best location to provide the coverage needed. Mr. Brimmer asked for clarification if there is written justification on the other locations considered. Mr. Powell answered in the affirmative and stated that this could be provided. Mr. Hill stated that this information was not provided as it is not required to be submitted with the request and there were locations that were not viable because of not being able to lease the property. Mr. Brimmer asked the amount of land needed for the cell tower. Mr. Hill answered that typically a 100x100 foot area is needed. Mr. Brimmer asked if any other locations on the golf course were considered. Mr. Hill answered that the cell tower needs to be in proximity to the residential neighborhoods to provide the service needed. Planning Committee

Mr. Smith stated that he is a resident of Rivertowne in Parkers Landing and is fully aware of the lack of service in the area. He stated that he is not opposed to accepting campaign contributions if offered, but has not previously accepted any campaign contributions from any telecommunication companies.

Mr. Smith moved to recommend to Town Council approval of the request. Mr. Carrier seconded the motion.

Mr. Brimmer stated that he has not taken campaign contributions from any telecommunication companies. He stated that he currently is in favor of the request and looks forward to seeing the justification that will be provided on the other locations that were considered. He stated that he reserves the right to change his vote based on that or any other information provided prior to or at Town Council. He stated that this is an important infrastructure and necessary service.

Mr. Bustos stated that he has not received any campaign contribution from telecommunication companies.

Mr. Brimmer called for a vote on the motion. All in favor.

The Committee convened for a short break at 4:10 pm and reconvened at 4:12 pm.

to amend the River Island Plantation Planned Development District Ordinance by allowing the erection, operation, and maintenance of a stealth wireless facility including a tower not to exceed 140 feet above ground level and related ground equipment as an allowed use on that 29.46 acre parcel designated as TMS No. 540-00-00-066. (Ord. No. 17039) Ms. Farrell stated that this is a request to amend the River Island Plantation Planned Development which is more familiar to most as Rivertowne. She stated that this is a proposal to amend this planned development specifically to allow a cellular tower not greater than 140 feet to be located in Rivertowne Country Club. She stated that this is straight forward and is to construct a cellular tower on a particular parcel of property and will not affect any of the other properties within Rivertowne and will be a permitted use so there are no other conditions. She stated that this was reviewed by the Planning Commission who held a public hearing, as well as the Planning Committee and both have unanimously recommended approval. Robert Newman, 1836 Delacourt Avenue, stated that he is a mechanical engineer and added that the cellular coverage in Rivertowne is very poor and unreliable. He stated that this is a serious safety issue for emergency situations and said that the cell tower is needed. He said that home extenders work slightly,

but do not work outside or out of range in your own home and do not work for visitors. He stated that residents who are worried about radiation from cellular towers do not understand that cellular tower signals are very weak which is why they are needed in so many areas. He said compare this weak radiation to radio and television transmitters at 100,000 watts that you are able to receive for hundreds of miles, and it does not compare to a cellular tower. Joe Daly, 2812 Parkers Landing Road, stated that he is on the Parkers Landing Board and also the President of Parkers Island Board and is very much in favor of the cellular tower. He added that the community really wants this tower, according to a survey they conducted. He stated that the location of the cellular tower is in the maintenance area of the golf course on 29 acres and in the best location possible. heart attack on the 4th fairway. He said that for this reason, he hopes that Council approves the cellular

request: Request to rezone from R-2, Low Density Residential District, to R-3, Medium Density Residential District. Property to remain in the SR2-OD, Special R-2 Overlay District. Location: 425 Bank Street Parcel ID (TMS No.): 532-05-00-128 Planning Commission

events.text:
Ms. Canon reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 2 & 3). Mr. Neal asked which properties are zoned R-2 in the surrounding area. Ms. Canon showed the zoning for the surrounding properties on the map for the Commission. Mr. Neal asked which properties are non-conforming. Ms. Canon answered that she did not have information on the exact number but based on the map it appeared there were multiple non-conforming lots.

Ms. Smith asked if redevelopment of the lot under R-2 zoning is precluded if the structure is removed. Ms. Canon answered in the negative and stated that any new structure would have to comply with the R-2 zoning standards and uses, which does not allow duplexes.

Mr. Wren asked if the property could be subdivided if it remained under the R- 3 zoning. Ms. Canon answered in the negative and stated that the units are attached. Mr. Wren asked if the adjacent public housing is still owned by the City of Charleston and if the zoning is R-2. Ms. Canon answered in the affirmative.

Mr. McNeill asked if the surrounding property is zoned R-2. Ms. Canon answered in the affirmative.

Ms. Campaigne asked if the adjacent property has apartments or duplexes. Ms. Canon answered she was unsure if they were multi-family or duplexes.

Mr. Nick Collins, representative for the applicant, reviewed the request with the Commission. He stated that the property was purchased with the duplex existing. He stated that because of fire and water damage, the entire structure needed to be demolished. He stated that they would like to rebuild the duplex and have similar affordable housing available.

Mr. Neal asked if it was previously a duplex. Mr. Collins answered in the affirmative and stated that it has been a duplex for the past 20 years. Mr. Neal asked if there are other duplexes in the area. Mr. Collins answered in the affirmative but was not sure of the exact location. Mr. Neal asked if the units would be affordable housing. Mr. Collins answered in the affirmative and stated that they do not intend to change the building from its original design. Planning Commission

There being no comments, Mr. Neal closed the public hearing.

Ms. Campaigne asked if the property is adjacent to apartments. Mr. Prause answered that he was not sure if the City of Charleston project pre-dates the R- 2 zoning designation. He reviewed the difference between townhouse, duplexes and apartments with the Commission. He stated that the zoning was designated in 1979.

Ms. Smith suggested that the apartments were existing before the zoning was established. She asked if it is required to bring a non-conforming lot into compliance if redeveloped. Mr. Neal answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Lehman asked if the duplex is “grandfathered in”. Mr. Prause answered that the use was allowed as non-conforming and would not have to be brought into compliance until after it met the 50% threshold. Mr. Lehman asked if this request was approved, would it set a precedence. Mr. Neal answered that there are apartments in the area and there are non-conforming lots as well. He suggested that there have been requests for subdivision of lots in the area with the desire to redevelop. He suggested that this changes the character of the neighborhood and he is not in favor of this. He stated that there have been occasions where rezoning was desired because it would mean a non-conforming use would then become conforming.

Ms. Smith suggested that subdivision was allowed when the lots met the lot requirements for the designated zoning.

Ms. Campaigne stated that she is in favor of having more affordable housing, but expressed concern with changing the zoning from what is seen with the surrounding neighborhood.

Ms. Gregg expressed concern with setting a precedent and that there would be subsequent similar requests.

Mr. Wren asked the difference between this property being in the overlay district and remaining zoned R-2. Ms. Canon answered that the overlay district allows reduction of the front setback. Planning Commission

Mr. Neal asked if this was denied, could there only be one unit on the lot. Mr. Prause answered in the affirmative and stated that there is a 40% lot coverage requirement.

Ms. Campaigne suggested that a single family unit could be constructed with an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) that could then be leased.

Ms. Smith moved for denial of the request. Mr. Millet seconded the motion.

Ms. Campaigne suggested that different structure types other than single family units should be considered to provide more affordable housing. She suggested that affordable housing is a critical issue and should be discussed during the update of the Comprehensive Plan.

Ms. Smith agreed but suggested that the current zoning should be taken into consideration. She suggested that approval of the request would set a precedent. She suggested that there is not a hardship for the request.

Mr. Neal suggested that there is a hardship in the fact that there was a fire and is in proximity to other apartments and multi-family units. He suggested that because there is no one at the meeting desiring to speak, there is no opposition to the request. He stated that he is in favor of more affordable housing.

Ms. Gregg suggested that this property not being in the historic district has a bearing on the involvement of the community. She suggested that the character is changing in this area because of not having the more stringent regulations.

Mr. Neal called for a vote on the motion. Motion passed on a 6 to 2 vote with Ms. Campaigne, Ms. Gregg, Mr. McNeill, Mr. Wren, Ms. Smith, and Mr. Lehman being in favor; Mr. Millet and Mr. Neal opposed.

Ms. Canon reviewed the request with the Committee (attachment 1). She stated that the Planning Commission recommended denial.

Mr. Carrier expressed concern with this request and having non-conforming structures. He stated that this is a recovering neighborhood and expressed concern with duplexes continuing to be allowed.

Mr. Carrier moved to recommend to Town Council denial of the request. Mr. Bustos seconded the motion. All in favor. Planning Committee

(Ord. No. 17047) Mr. Gawrych moved for approval; seconded by Mr. Smith. Mr. Santos asked Ms. Farrell what can be built on Areawide Business and what can be built on what is being requested for the change in zoning. Ms. Farrell stated that Areawide Business is the requested zoning. She said this property is currently unincorporated so they are requesting to incorporate and zone Areawide Business. She said that it is a variety of different retail, office types of uses, because this is in the Urban Corridor and there is an allowance for some residential. She said it is a broad spectrum of uses, but not the more intense types of uses such as auto repair. Mr. Santos asked if a hotel could be built. Ms. Farrell responded in the affirmative. Mr. Santos asked if the properties adjacent to this property are also zoned as such, could a hotel go on their property as well. Ms. Farrell stated that this is the next item on the agenda, which is to request Areawide Business zoning for those properties as well. Mr. Santos stated that this is something that needs to be looked at, because many of the citizens are talking about hotels. He said

that Charleston has slowed down on building hotels and the Town appears to be building more. He added that the Comprehensive Plan Committee also needs to look at this when discussing the Comprehensive Plan. He said putting together these properties is going to provide an opportunity to build another big hotel and traffic and infrastructure needs to be reviewed in that area. He said that this is a very busy intersection and he and the citizens are concerned about this. Sean Barnes, 1418 Barbara Street, said that he is a local businessman and has been in business for 28 years. He said that he is the owner of Docks Unlimited and owns two lots on the right hand side. He added that he has a long-term lease on 1361 Old Georgetown Highway and owns the other lot. He said he builds docks and does aluminum fabrication. He said where Larry’s Locks used to be to the tip of that property is going to be a hotel. He said that it has already been purchased. He said that there is a gentleman that lives two blocks over that has a steel building and is not able to do anything with it, so he purchased it. He said since the new overlay, you are not able to build on your property until you are 75 feet off on one side and 50 feet back from Old Georgetown Highway. He said that he has been working on this property for a long time, but when the roadwork was redone, it took away the exit point and did a roundabout. He said now they have done something completely different and he is unable to turn around with a regular vehicle, so a firetruck cannot turn around. He said they allow them to cut through into the Old K- Mart, but this is not a real road. He asked how an outlet or access could be put in. Barry Wolff, 1468 Pocahontas Street said that this is part and parcel of what he said before in regards to the public not understanding the ramifications of the zoning. He said if the public was aware that these parcels were possibly being consolidated for the construction of another hotel, Council Chambers would be full.

Gary Berenyi, of Hoyt and Berenyi, said that this rezoning is consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and the intention is not to build a hotel, but an office/retail space/flex space and to have some flexibility which is consistent with everything in that area. Mr. Santos was opposed. All other present voted in favor. Mr. DeMoura read FIRST READING BY TITLE ONLY. 4.

to rezone from NC, Neighborhood Commercial District, to AB, Areawide Business District, an approximately 0.39 acre tract of land located at 1375 Old Georgetown Road, identified by TMS No. 559-13-00-027, and depicted as a portion of Lot 8 on a plat recorded by the Charleston

County RMC Office in Book G, Page 049. Property to remain in the UC-OD, Urban Corridor Overlay District. (Ord. No. 17055) Ms. Farrell stated that this property is under half an acre and located on Georgetown Road behind the new Bowman Place Shopping Center and is included within the Urban Corridor Overlay District (UCOD), so the request to rezone from NC to AB has been recommended for approval by both the Planning Commission and the Planning Committee. Mr. Bustos asked if either zoning would allow for hotels in this area. Ms. Farrell responded in the affirmative. She said that NC does allow for a hotel, but is limited to a boutique hotel of no more than 50 rooms. She said that AB would allow for any size hotel; however, because the property is included in the UCOD, this expands those permitted uses that are found within the NC district to be those that are in the AB. She stated that it eliminates the boutique hotel option and any size hotel could potentially be built there. Mr. Owens stated that it appears that the same owner owns the five parcels there. He said that it appears that you could erase the lines and have one large parcel of property. Ms. Farrell stated that she believes this is the intent, but does not know for what purpose. She stated that there have been no submittals or applications for this. She stated that if the owner wanted to abandon those property lines, this would be a piece of property with zoning lines that do not match up to any property lines. Mayor Haynie asked how large the property would be if all those parcels are put together. Ms. Farrell stated that all the parcels are all similar in size, with one being slightly larger, which would be approximately two acres.

Mayor Haynie stated that if Council does not approve this, what may be the intended uses for this property. Ms. Farrell stated that it would not affect it, because it is part of the UCOD and the use of a hotel would still be a permitted use. She stated that this is more administrative to clean up in order not to end up with underlying zoning districts that do not match any property line. She said that it will not change the permitted uses, because it is already part of the overlay. Mr. Santos stated that the urban corridor needs to be reviewed on Chuck Dawley Boulevard, because more and more hotels are being built. He stated there is a small street that is going to service that area with a dead end at the other end. He said that there will be one way in and one way out and will be right on Bowman Road. He said even if they did have an exit on the other side, there is the car rental place and does not see this as a way to get in and out with access to Johnnie Dodds Boulevard without causing additional traffic. He said he would like for the Planning Committee to take another look at the Urban Corridor on Chuck Dawley Boulevard to see if this should be removed. He said this scares him to have a big hotel going in across the street from two other new hotels. Ms. Farrell stated that the Urban Corridor is broken up into three sections; Coleman/Ben Sawyer; Johnnie Dodds; and Chuck Dawley. She said this is part of the Johnnie Dodds sections and the Chuck Dawley is the least intense of the three sections. She said that Johnnie Dodds has the greater building height and more expansive uses. Mr. Santos stated that it does not have access to Johnnie Dodds. Ms. Farrell stated that this is how the map was drawn. Mr. Santos stated that this will add to traffic on Bowman Road. He asked that the Planning Committee review this again and ensure that all this will fit.

Mr. Bustos stated that this may be a great place to begin the discussion of a hotel district, because h

Mr. Bustos asked if the request is located within a zoning district that allows hotels. Mr. Ulma answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Brimmer suggested this is an example of how the different zoning districts should be reviewed to determine where hotels would be appropriate.

Ms. Whitley asked if the Urban Corridor allows larger hotels. Mr. Bustos answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Bustos asked about height. Mr. DeMoura answered that the maximum height is 80 feet.

Mr. O’Rourke moved to recommend to Town Council approval of final reading of the request. Mr. Brimmer seconded the motion. All in favor.

to rezone from NC, Neighborhood Commercial District, to AB, Areawide Business District, an approximately 0.39 acre tract of land located at 1375 Old Georgetown Road, identified by TMS No. 559-13-00-027, and depicted as a portion of Lot 8 on a plat recorded by the Charleston County RMC Office in Book G, Page 049. No. 17055) Mr. Ulma said that this request was deferred that involves a change from Neighborhood Commercial to Areawide Business. request: Request approval of Waiver from Land Development Regulations (LDR), Section 155.047, and approval of Sketch Plan for Lieben Forest Subdivision, 18 SF Residential Lots zoned R-3, Medium Density Residential District, located at Lieben Road. Parcel ID (TMS No.): 614-00-00-025

events.text:
Mr. Bernard reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 2 & 3).

Mr. Neal asked about sidewalks and the kiosk. Mr. Bernard answered that there are only sidewalks on one side and staff recommends that the kiosk be moved to a more central location.

Mr. McNeill asked about lot 17 in regard to tree removal. Mr. Bernard answered that it is in the middle of a ditch and the lot.

Ms. Campaigne asked which lots are included in the waiver request. Mr. Bernard answered that it is lots 9-18.

Mr. Wofford Stribling, Earthsource Engineering, reviewed the request with the Commission. He stated that they are amenable with all comments with the exception of #5 regarding tree preservation. He stated that they may need to preserve tree #22. He asked that tree #77 and #92 be allowed to be removed.

Mr. Neal asked the intention of the green area behind lots 15-18. He expressed concern that this would not be used as green space but would be included in the lots. Mr. Stribling answered that it would be HOA property with the potential for a future trail. Mr. Neal asked about sidewalks and if sidewalks Planning Commission

could be included on both sides of the street. Mr. Stribling answered that they are trying to limit the amount of impact to the jurisdictional wetlands. He stated that they are willing to further work with staff on this issue. Ms. Gregg asked if having lots 14-18 deeper would provide more tree preservation. Mr. Stribling answered that the current lot configuration would allow for more preservation of trees.

Mr. Neal asked if the drainage easement configuration is typical. Mr. Mitchell answered that it was probably configured to avoid conflicts with other utilities and the drainage for the rest of the subdivision drainage. Mr. Neal asked if there is another alternative. Mr. Mitchell answered in the affirmative.

Ms. Campaigne suggested that a reduction of lots could be considered so that there was sufficient drainage and tree preservation.
