label: Location: 1236 Melvin Bennett Road
request: Case #R-03-18, Rezone from R-1, Low Density Residential District, to AB-2, Areawide Business-2 District; Amend the Comprehensive Plan 2009-2019 (2014 Update) Future Land Use Map by changing the land use designation from Low Density Neighborhood to Commercial located at Location: 1236 Melvin Bennett Road (Melvin Bennett / Bowman Rd). TMS No.: 560-02-00- 038; 560-02-00-039 and 560-02-00-019 (portions thereof)

events.text:
Ms. Canon reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1&2). Planning Commission

Ms. Smith suggested that the applicant has not indicated any plans for the portion fronting Bowman Road. Ms. Canon answered that the property is requested to be AB-2 for the portion fronting Bowman Road.

Mr. Wren asked if additional action would be needed from the Commission. Ms. Canon answered in the negative.

Ms. Smith asked if AB would be more appropriate than AB-2. Ms. Canon answered that the Comprehensive Plan future land use recommends commercial zoning, so either district is compatible with the commercial land use.

Mr. Neal suggested that AB-2 would be appropriate since there is property adjacent that is AB-2.

Ms. Smith asked if the R-1 portion was subdivided would it meet minimum standards. Ms. Canon answered that this would be determined when a subdivision request was submitted.

Mr. Tim Askins reviewed the request with the Commission. He stated that the intention is to subdivide the portion along Melvin Bennett into two lots with open space between each parcel.

Mr. Wren asked about curb cut on Bowman Road. Mr. Askins answered that SCDOT has approved a curb cut for the property.

Ms. Gregg asked about buffers. Mr. Askins answered that the buffers would meet or exceed Town requirements.

Mr. Millet asked if there are homes on the adjacent lots and where access is located. Ms. Canon answered that access for the adjacent properties is from Melvin Bennett. Planning Commission

Mr. Sean Rudy, 1232 Melvin Bennett, stated that he was not contacted regarding this project. He stated that the area is heavily wooded. He expressed concern with family and child safety. He stated that safety and security is a major concern. He suggested that the property should remain residential.

Mr. John Burn, 1411 Breckon Road, suggested that the zoning request is appropriate. He suggested that because of traffic, it would not be appropriate to have residential dwellings on Bowman Road.

Ms. Melanie Ensminger, 1244 Melvin Bennett, expressed concern with drainage as problems currently exist. She expressed additional concern with tree removal and noise. She stated that this is one of the oldest neighborhoods in the Town and suggested that the character of the neighborhood should be preserved.

Mr. Paul Taylor, 1336 Bluebird Drive, agreed that the portion fronting Bowman Road is appropriate as well as having residential lots fronting Melvin Bennett. He expressed concern with traffic. He asked if green space was included in the project, who would own the green space and what the width of the green space would be.

Mr. Terry Orvig, 1334 Blue Bird, stated that he is not opposed to commercial property, but is concerned with commercial property in proximity to residential. He stated that as one of the oldest neighborhoods, the character of the neighborhood should be preserved. He suggested that the growth of the Town should be maintained. He stated that he is opposed to the request. He expressed concern with property values being affected.

Mr. Matt Schrimm, 1440 Melvin Bennett, expressed concern with commercial property affecting his property as it is adjacent to the proposed property. He expressed concern with tree removal as there are a significant number of historic trees on the property. He expressed concern with drainage and stated that there is currently significant drainage problems. He expressed concern with having additional fill on the lot. He expressed concern with what type of buffer would be required between the commercial and residential property. Planning Commission

Ms. Mamie Rudy, 1232 Melvin Bennett, expressed concern with the proposed commercial portion would back up to their residence. She expressed concern with child safety. She stated that there is a huge historic oak on the property and does not want the tree to be removed or impacted.

Mr. Kevin Cunnane, 3032 River Vista Way, suggested that the entire area in regard to flooding and character should be taken into consideration.

There being no further comments, Mr. Wren closed the public hearing.

Mr. Askins stated that he intends to have water and sewer for the property and there would be a drainage plan. He stated that he intends to preserve the historic oak trees as well.

Mr. McNeill asked where the drainage pipe would be located. Mr. Askins answered that he would tie in from Chuck Dawley Blvd.

Mr. Millet asked if the property could be subdivided and preserve the existing trees. Mr. Askins answered in the affirmative. Mr. Millet asked what type of commercial is proposed. Mr. Askins answered that the specific commercial use has not been finalized.

Ms. Gregg asked if the oak trees would be preserved on the proposed commercial property. Mr. Askins answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Neal asked if the subdivision would be reviewed by staff or the Commission. Ms. Canon answered that a sketch plan would be needed. She stated that this is a zoning request and that a sketch plan cannot be considered at this time. Mr. Neal stated that the adjacent residential property already backs up to AB-2 property. He stated that a drainage plan would be required and would be reviewed by staff. He suggested that the current issue is the zoning request. Mr. Neal asked how many lots could be accomplished with the current zoning. Ms. Canon answered that approximately five lots could be accomplished. Planning Commission

Ms. Campaigne asked about the 25 foot bufferyard proposed and if this would exceed the requirements. Ms. Canon answered in the negative and stated that a minimum 25 foot buffer would be required. Ms. Campaigne asked if the buffer between commercial and residential would be more substantial than if it was residential adjacent to other residential. Ms. Canon answered that no buffer would be required between single family uses. Ms. Campaigne suggested that having commercial use with a buffer would better preserve the wooded character and “feel” of the lot and surrounding area as it currently exists than if there were only residential uses.

Mr. McNeill suggested that the proposed changes to the tree and buffer ordinance would mean greater tree protection if approved.

Mr. Millet suggested that the questions asked by the Commission are to try to better understand the request and thanked the Commission for those inquiries. He stated that the Comprehensive Plan identified commercial nodes, but many of those areas were rezoned or were developed as residential. He stated that this means that the commercial must developed elsewhere and sometimes is next to residential. He stated that the property would be developed and suggested that it could be more intensive with more residential units than what is proposed.

Ms. Smith expressed concern with this request at the same time of updating the Comprehensive Plan and suggested that it might not be appropriate to entertain this request at this time. She suggested that this should be addressed during the Comprehensive Plan update.

Mr. Neal stated that the Comprehensive Plan already recommends commercial and suggested that this would not change with the Comprehensive Plan update.

Ms. Canon clarified that the request includes a Comprehensive Plan update and reviewed this with the Commission.

Mr. Wren asked if there is concern with split zoning a parcel. Mr. Pagliarini answered that the application clarifies the request and what zoning is requested Planning Commission

for the specific portion of the property. Ms. Canon agreed and stated that there is a zoning plan included with the request that clarifies where the commercial and residential zoning would be located. She stated that a sketch plan would be required with the subdivision of the property following the lines of the zoning map.

Ms. Gregg asked if there is follow-up on drainage plans to ensure the appropriate drainage is installed. Ms. Canon answered that staff would have certain inspections that would be required prior to certificate of occupancy (CO). Mr. Bernard agreed.

Mr. Cuttino moved for approval including all staff comments. Ms. Campaigne seconded the motion. Motion passed on a 7 to 2 vote with Ms. Campaigne, Ms. Gregg, Mr. McNeill, Mr. Wren, Mr. Lehman, Mr. Neal and Mr. Cuttino in favor; Ms. Smith and Mr. Millet opposed.

thereof), and depicted on a plat recorded in the Charleston County ROD Office in Plat Book BA-179, Page 179 and Plat Book CE, Page 190.

Ms. Melanie Ensminger, 1244 Melvin Bennett, stated that she has reviewed the plans with the applicant. She suggested that this is setting a precedent for the surrounding area. She expressed concern with preservation of trees, buffers and child safety. She expressed concern with the portion fronting Bowman Road being zoned commercial. She stated that her understanding is that the entire parcel would be rezoned AB-2 with a portion fronting Melvin Bennett being rezoned to R-1 at a later date.

Mr. Ulma reviewed the request with the Committee (attachment 1).

Mr. Bustos asked for clarification on what would be rezoned to AB-2. Mr. Ulma showed the portion being rezoned on the map for the Committee and explained that the change only applied to the portion of the property fronting on Bowman Road. Mr. Bustos asked if the remaining property would remain R-1. Mr. Ulma answered in the affirmative. Mr. Bustos asked if the AB-2 would only apply to the portion of the property depicted. Mr. Ulma answered in the affirmative. Mr. Bustos asked when the property would be subdivided. Mr. Tim Askins answered that the existing home would need to be demolished before the property could be subdivided.

Mr. O’Rourke asked where Ms. Ensminger and Ms. Rudy’s properties are located. They indicated the location on the map for the Committee.

Mr. Brimmer expressed concern with rezoning to AB-2 and suggested that AB zoning would be more appropriate. He suggested that a less intensive commercial use should be considered to “transition” as you travel down Bowman Road. Mr. Askins stated that the request would be in keeping with the adjacent commercial.

Mr. Brimmer moved to recommend to Town Council denial of the zoning request. Ms. Whitely seconded the motion. Motion passed on a 3 to 1 vote with Mr. Brimmer, Ms. Whitley, and Mr. O’Rourke in favor; Mr. Bustos opposed.

Mr. Bustos suggested that the requested zoning is appropriate and there is traditionally less intensive uses along Bowman Road. Planning Committee

Mr. Brimmer suggested that the Comprehensive Plan amendment should not be considered at this time.

request: SP-01-18—Request approval of Sketch Plan for two single-family residential lots. Also request approval for Waiver from Land Development Regulations, located at 2839 North Highway 17 / Located between Yough Hall Road and Crystal Drive. TMS No.: 578-00-00-121 Planning Commission

events.text:
Mr. Mitchell reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2).

Mr. Wren asked if there is currently no buffer requirement. Mr. Mitchell answered that it is under the purview of the Commission to determine if a buffer should be required. Mr. Wren asked if it was a commercial use would the Commission determine the buffer. Mr. Mitchell answered in the negative and stated that Design Review Board would have purview over the buffer for a commercial use.

Mr. Neal asked who would be responsible for maintaining the roadway. Mr. Mitchell answered that it would be a private roadway.

Mr. Lewis Seabrook, surveyor for the applicant, reviewed the request with Commission.

Mr. Neal asked how the road would be maintained. Mr. Seabrook answered that this has not been determined to date but would ensure a maintenance agreement in perpetuity was put in place prior to final plat approval.

Mr. Wren asked if the existing home would remain. Mr. Seabrook answered in the affirmative. Mr. Wren suggested that front portion could potentially be commercial and asked if the applicant would be opposed to having a 50-foot buffer. Mr. Seabrook answered in the negative and stated that there is currently a 30-foot easement along US17.

Mr. Millet asked what material the driveway would be. Mr. Seabrook answered that it would be a combination of rock and dirt. Mr. Millet asked if the property was requested not to be included in the overlay district when annexed. Ms. Canon answered that an overlay district is not automatically assigned at the time of annexation; it must be requested.

Mr. Pagliarini asked if there is an existing access easement. Mr. Seabrook answered in the negative. Mr. Pagliarini asked if the current rendering shows the access easement extending across the property line. Mr. Seabrook answered in the affirmative and stated that there is also a SCDOT curb at the proposed access from US17. Planning Commission

Ms. Gregg asked if both lots would be conforming. Mr. Seabrook answered in the negative. Mr. Seabrook also noted that the property currently has septic. He stated that sewer service is desired, so annexation must be requested.

Mr. Neal expressed concern with the access extending across the property line and how this could be remedied. Mr. Mitchell answered that the easement would be on the property line. Mr. Pagliarini stated that an easement does not currently exist, only a driveway.

Mr. McNeill asked where the curb cut is located. Mr. Mitchell showed the location on the plat for the Commission. Mr. McNeill asked if the two properties would share the existing curb cut. Mr. Pagliarini answered that an additional easement might be necessary as well.

Ms. Campaigne suggested that the easement would be on the requested property. Ms. Smith agreed and stated that the driveway would need to be moved. Mr. Mitchell agreed.

Ms. Gregg asked if the easement would be recorded. Mr. Mitchell answered in the affirmative and suggested that other elements as noted in the staff comments should be included on the plat as well. Ms. Gregg asked if there is a way to have both future parcels conforming. Mr. Mitchell answered in the negative.

Mr. Millet asked what is adjacent to the requested parcel. Mr. Mitchell answered there is a car wash on the south parcel and the north parcel is vacant. Mr. Millet asked if there is access to the car wash. Mr. Mitchell answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Neal moved for approval of the request including all staff comments with the added condition that a satisfactory easement and access plan in accordance with Town roadway standards to be approved by the Transportation Department. Mr. Cuttino seconded the motion.

Mr. Neal asked if Fire Department approval would be needed prior to the Transportation Department giving final approval for the roadway. Mr. Mitchell answered that the information and all approvals are provided prior to approval of the final plat. Planning Commission

Ms. Campaigne asked about buffers. Mr. Neal suggested that the buffer is included in the staff comments. Mr. Mitchell stated that staff noted that if a buffer was desired, it should be included in the approval.

Ms. Smith moved to amend the motion to establish a 50-foot buffer along US17 for the newly created lot. Mr. Wren seconded the amendment.

Mr. McNeill suggested that there is currently a 30 foot easement and asked if the buffer would be outside of the easement.

Ms. Campaigne suggested that the buffer should include the easement.

Mr. McNeill suggested that if the property were commercial, a 20-foot buffer outside of the easement might not be sufficient.

Mr. Neal suggested that a larger buffer would be too onerous.

Ms. Gregg asked if the requested buffer width is standard.

Mr. Wren asked what the buffer requirements are. Mr. Mitchell answered that it would be 100 foot width for major arterials with a minimum 50 feet width for collector streets and minor arterials.

Mr. Millet asked for clarification on the requested buffer and if the 50 foot buffer requirement would include the easement. Mr. Wren answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Wren called for a vote on the amendment. Motion passed on a 7 to 2 vote with Ms. Campaigne, Ms. Gregg, Mr. Wren, Ms. Smith, Mr. Lehman, Mr. Millet and Mr. Cuttino in favor; Mr. McNeill and Mr. Neal opposed.

Mr. Wren called for a vote on the amended motion. All in favor. Planning Commission

label: 651 McCants Drive / Corner of McCants Dr
request: SP-02-18—Request approval of Sketch Plan for 10 single-family residential lots, located at 651 McCants Drive / Corner of McCants Dr. & Jackson St. TMS No.: 532-10-00-001

events.text:
Mr. Mitchell and Mr. Bernard reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2).

Mr. McNeill asked about lots 4-9 and if access would be from Jackson Street. Mr. Mitchell answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Wren asked about access for lot 10. Mr. Mitchell answered that it would be from the easement (hatched section).

Mr. Cuttino asked about the trees near lot 7 and lot 9. Mr. Bernard answered that they are a laurel oak and live oak.

Mr. McNeill asked who owns the right-of-way. Mr. Bernard answered that they are state streets.

Ms. Campaigne suggested that SCDOT approval could be stipulated in the motion.

Mr. John Tarkin reviewed the request with the Commission. He stated that they would like to preserve as many trees as possible including some pine trees that have sentimental value.

Mr. Millet asked if the applicant would be amenable to having a sidewalk on Jackson Street. Mr. Tarkin answered that he is not opposed to a sidewalk, but if constructed, the sidewalk would not connect to an existing sidewalk and would mean significant trees would need to be removed.

Ms. Smith stated that staff did not recommend a sidewalk on Jackson Street and suggested that impervious surface should not be increased in this area.

Mr. Wren asked if the trees in the right-of-way can be preserved. Mr. Tarkin noted that tree removal is not necessary for installation of driveways. Mr. Tony Wooddy answered that the main reason for the laurel oak and live oak are being proposed for removal is because of installation of a sewer line. He stated that Planning Commission

the trees would be preserved if possible but wanted to have the option in the event they needed to be removed.

Mr. Neal asked about the laurel oak by the easement for lot 10 as well as the other trees between lot 9 and the easement and asked if they can be better preserved. Mr. Tarkin answered that the easement is 20 feet wide, but the driveway would only be twelve feet wide and would have pervious material of sand shell or plantation mix. He stated that the rendering shows a more meandering driveway so that the trees are not as impacted. Mr. Neal suggested that the lot 9 property line should be moved so that the trees fall within the HOA property and preserved. Mr. Tarkin answered that this could be done.

Ms. Campaigne commended the applicant on the smart design and the preservation of the trees for the property. Mr. Tarkin stated that they would mitigate all of the protected trees removed but would like to preserve as many trees as possible. He stated that there is a bio-swale and garden to the rear of the property that would carry runoff to the dry pond.

Mr. Wren asked about the trees not included on the submittal. Mr. Wooddy answered that the original tree survey had some incorrectly labeled trees. He stated that the revised tree survey is correct.

Mr. Wooddy reviewed the reasoning for the LDR waiver request with the Commission. ➢ Topography and pattern of the lots—there is a natural low area near lot 10 and significant trees. He stated that rather than regrade the area that would alter the drainage pattern and impact the protected trees, the access easement was determined the best option. ➢ Detrimental to adjacent property—He stated that the only property not developed is to the north and a pipe drainage easement is being provided for future development. ➢ Protecting health, safety, and welfare—He stated that the storm drainage system along Jackson Street flows into the low area of this property. He stated that improvements proposed would increase the storm coverage to 50% which is above the required percentage.

Mr. Neal asked the width of lots 5-8 compared to lot 9. Mr. Tarkin answered that lot 9 is approximately 20 feet wider than the other lots. Planning Commission

Ms. Gregg asked if lot 5 and 6 are buildable given the canopy of the protected tree. Mr. Tarkin answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Wren asked how the Old Village drainage study improvements would impact this property. Mr. Mitchell answered that the property is within the Royall Avenue basin and there would be improvements in the near future in the area including along Jackson Street.

Mr. Cuttino asked about landscaping and how it would be maintained. Mr. Tarkin answered that it would be maintained by the HOA.

Mr. McNeill asked how the maintenance would be accomplished. Mr. Neal suggested that the property could be deed restricted through the HOA.

Ms. Campaigne moved for approval including staff comments; emphasizing the desire for the applicant to work with staff so trees currently shown on lot 9 are protected by adjusting the lot line between lot 9 and the proposed easement with final approval by staff. Mr. Neal seconded the motion.

Mr. Neal asked if the motion is intended to have the trees located in the HOA property. Ms. Campaigne answered in the negative and stated that she would not want the better quality trees to be potentially impacted because of moving the lot line.

Mr. Wren amended the motion to include preservation of trees 54 and 39 with SCDOT approval. Mr. Neal seconded the motion.

Mr. Neal asked how the motion can be amended when the trees are in an SCDOT right-of-way. Mr. Pagliarini answered that this cannot be done and therefore the amendment is not valid.

Mr. Wren withdrew his amendment. Mr. Neal withdrew his second.

Mr. Neal asked if motion includes sidewalks on Jackson Street. Ms. Campaigne answered in the negative.

Mr. Wren called for a vote on the motion. All in favor. Planning Commission

label: 3745 North Highway 17
request: R-05-18 Annex and zone one parcel PI-2, Public Institutional-2 District, located at 3745 North Highway 17 (Town Property at Lieben Road). TMS No.: 614-00-00-033

events.text:
Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2).

Mr. Jody Peele stated that the Town is in the process of securing a consultant to complete a Public Services master plan.

Ms. Smith suggested that it would be beneficial for the Town to reach out to the community to provide more information on what is proposed in the future, transportation issues, etc. Mr. Peele answered that a better idea of how the property would be utilized would be known once the master plan was completed. He stated that there are no plans to use this property as a transfer yard.

Mr. Neal asked if it is beneficial to defer annexation and zoning until the master plan is completed. Mr. Peele answered that they would like to complete the master plan based on the ordinances in place for the property and that it would be better to have it annexed and zoned within the Town.

Ms. Gregg asked what current activities are being conducted on Six Mile site. Mr. Peele answered that there are five divisions working out of the Six Mile Facility: stormwater, waste management, facilities, grounds, and infrastructure. Ms. Gregg asked what a transfer yard entails. Mr. Peele answered that all garbage goes to a landfill or commercial drop-off site. He stated that any vegetative material is transported to the Six Mile Facility, reloaded and then transported to the Bees Ferry landfill. He stated that by doing this, it keeps as many vehicles in Mount Pleasant working throughout the Town.

Mr. Darien Mackey, 3605 Purple Martin, asked if the requested property would be used as a transfer station. Mr. Wren answered that it was indicated that it would not be used as a transfer yard.

Ms. Tamarae Tabaka, 3774 Copahee Sound Dr, expressed concern with the property being used for a dump site and that it would be detrimental to the Planning Commission

quality of life for the surrounding neighborhood. She stated that Lieben Road is a narrow two-lane road with no signal onto Hwy 17. She asked that the property be buffered and screened. She asked that the main entrance of the property be located off Hwy 17 and not on Lieben Road and that a signal be added to the intersection of Lieben Road and Hwy 17 as well.

Ms. Charlotte Pollard, 1558 Periwinkle Dr, expressed concern with there being increased truck traffic, particularly with the proximity of Wando High School. She suggested that Lieben Road is the “jumping off point” of a cultural corridor and suggested that this would not be an ideal location for this type of use.

Mr. David Tabaka, 3774 Copahee Sound Dr, suggested that it is premature to approve this request since it is not known how the property would be used.

Mr. John Frahalla, 1530 Macoma Dr, expressed concern with their only being one access from Hwy 17 to the entire neighborhood. He suggested that the zoning should not be determined until the master plan is completed. He stated that it is a pedestrian-friendly neighborhood. He stated that there is only one access into the neighborhood and expressed concern with having a commercial use at the front of the neighborhood.

Mr. Edward Tabor, 3767 Tipp Lane, agreed with previous comments and expressed concern with increased truck traffic in the neighborhood, particularly with the potential for increased truck traffic in proximity of the schools.

There being no further comments, Mr. Wren closed the public hearing.

Mr. Neal asked if the transportation concerns can be addressed through the completion of the master plan including buffers, screening, increased truck traffic, etc. He also asked if the property is annexed but the zoning denied, what would the default zoning. Mr. Peele answered that the property has already been purchased. Mr. Rutherford answered that the property would be zoned R-1 which does not allow outdoor storage. Mr. Neal asked if there are plans to use the property within the next 60-90 days. Mr. Peele answered that the Public Services Department does not have any plans for the property at this time, but the property is currently being utilized by the Fire and Police Departments. Planning Commission

Ms. Campaigne expressed confidence in the Town being able to address all concerns. She stated that there is a difference in the county requirements from the Town requirements and suggested that there is a risk that the master plan would have to be redesigned if completed under the county requirements.

Mr. McNeill asked if there are any other options than PI-2. Ms. Canon answered in the negative and stated that this is the most compatible zoning for future use of the property. Mr. McNeill asked if it would be used as a transfer yard. Mr. Peele answered that the proposed property is not large enough to support a transfer yard and the Six Mile facility is more centrally located and serves the Town well.

Mr. Millet asked if any other location has been considered. Mr. Peele answered that this property was purchased with the thought that it would be the best location to serve the community. Mr. Millet suggested that the requested zoning does not fit the community. Mr. Peele stated that the master plan would determine what uses are located at that location. Mr. Millet suggested that the master plan should be determined before moving forward. Mr. Peele noted that the Six Mile facility is located within a residential area and works well within a mainly residential area. He stated that it will take some time to determine the master plan and what would be located on the property. He stated that at this time, he does not have any concrete plans. He stated that the property was purchased to provide a location to better serve the Town in that area.

Mr. Wren asked how many dwellings could be located on the property if it were zoned R-1 residential. Mr. Rutherford answered that it could allow approximately 15 homes. Ms. Canon noted that the future land use recommends Public Institutional (PI), so a Comprehensive Plan amendment would be needed to establish density if zoned differently. Mr. Wren asked if the requested zoning was denied, would the zoning then be non-conforming based on the Future Land Use Map and Comprehensive Plan. Ms. Canon answered in the affirmative.

Ms. Smith suggested that this move forward, with the Town working with the community as the master plan is completed.

Mr. Neal stated that this would be a recommendation to Town Council and asked what the next step would be on the design so that the public can provide Planning Commission

input. Mr. Rutherford answered that property zoned PI does not require Design Review Board approval; it would be reviewed and approved by staff.

Mr. Neal moved for approval including all staff comments. Mr. McNeill seconded the motion.

Mr. Neal strongly encouraged the Town to involve the community in the development of the master plan going forward. Mr. Peele answered that this could be done.

Mr. Wren called for a vote on the motion. All in favor.

Ms. Smith moved to amend the agenda to discuss item 6D next. Mr. Neal seconded the motion. As a point of order, Mr. Pagliarini stated that the agenda could not be amended; therefore, the motion could not be made.

Mr. Terry McManus, 1534 Periwinkle Dr, expressed concern with the proposed uses for the property once it is annexed and rezoned. He asked that the community be kept informed of what is planned for the property. He stated that they are concerned that the proposed uses would increase traffic in the area.

Mr. Brimmer asked the reason for the resolution. Mr. Ulma answered that this is required for annexation of Town-owned property.

Ms. Sally Jacob, 1152 Village Creek Lane, expressed concern with the PI-2 zoning and what the uses would entail. He suggested that if it is to be used for residential, affordable housing should be considered.

Mr. John Brahalla, 1530 Macoma Drive, expressed concern with the allowed uses associated with the proposed zoning and what the budget for the project would be. Mr. DeMoura answered that this would be an expansion of the critical services that are provided by the Town at the Six Mile Facility. Planning Committee

He stated that this is an industrial area that was purchased by the Town for industrial uses. He stated that it would be used for an extension of the Public Services Department.

Mr. Ulma reviewed the request with the Committee (attachment 1).

Mr. Brimmer asked if all three can be taken in one motion. Mr. DeMoura answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Brimmer moved to recommend to Town Council approval of items 5a.1, 5a.2, and 5a.3. Mr. O’Rourke seconded the motion. All in favor.

providing for the annexation of an approximately 5.32 acre tract of land owned by the Town of Mount Pleasant, located at 3745 Highway 17 North, identified by TMS No. 614-00-00-033 and depicted as Lot 1 on a plat recorded by the Charleston County ROD Office in Plat Book L10, Page 0138. (Ord. No. 18025) Mr. Bustos made a motion to approve Item #2 for an annexation; seconded by Mr. Owens. All present voted in favor. Mr. DeMoura read FIRST READING BY TITLE ONLY. 3.

to zone PI-2, Public Institutional-2 District, an approximately 5.32 acre tract of land owned by the Town of Mount Pleasant, located at 3745 Highway 17 North, identified by TMS No. 614-00-00-033 and depicted as Lot 1 on a plat recorded by the Charleston County ROD Office in Plat Book L10, Page 0138. (Ord. No. 18026) Mr. Bustos made a motion to zone PI-2, Public Institutional-2 District; seconded by Mr. Brimmer. Mayor Haynie stated that this is the former Berkeley Electric property up in the north portion of the Town and will be our Operations Center. He stated that the Town is working on a master plan for this Operations Center. Mr. Santos thanked Mayor Haynie for advising the public. He thinks in the future, that information should be put on the agenda, so the general public understands what is being voted on. Mr. Cunnane stated that he would also like to note that there was a sizeable contingent of nearby residents that were interested in this property at the Planning Commission. He added that Mr. Jody Peele provided the residents with assurances that it will not be a transfer station. He said the residents were not necessarily opposed but were concerned. He stated that he would like to put on the record that the concerns of those citizens are noted and what Mr. Peele mentioned at the Planning Commission hearing should be part of Council’s consideration as well, which is that the

residents do not want dumping or that type of activity happening on that property. He said there were a number of residents from that area that attended the Planning Commission meeting. All present voted in favor. Mr. DeMoura read FIRST READING BY TITLE ONLY. 4.

providing for the annexation of an approximately 5.32 acre tract of land owned by the Town of Mount Pleasant, located at 3745 Highway 17 North, identified by TMS No. 614-00-00-033 and depicted as Lot 1 on a plat recorded by the Charleston County ROD Office in Plat Book L10, Page 0138. (Ord. No. 18025) [Mr. Bustos departed the meeting at 7:37 p.m.] Mr. Ulma stated that the next two items are final reading for the annexation and zoning of Town owned property at Lieben Road and Highway 17 North, which will be studied for future use by Public Services Department. The current zoning in the County is Community Commercial and the Planning Committee recommended approval of the annexation. Mr. Santos moved for approval; seconded by Mr. Owens. 2.

to zone PI-2, Public Institutional-2 District, an approximately 5.32 acre tract of land owned by the Town of Mount Pleasant, located at 3745 Highway 17 North, identified by TMS No. 614-00-00-033 and depicted as Lot 1 on a plat recorded by the Charleston County ROD Office in Plat Book L10, Page 0138. (Ord. No. 18026) Mr. Santos moved for approval; seconded by Mr. Brimmer. All present voted in favor. (Mr. Bustos was not present for the vote) Mr. DeMoura read FINAL READING BY TITLE ONLY. This Ordinance SIGNED, SEALED and DELIVERED this date. 3.

request: R-06-18 Annex and zone R-4, Medium Density Residential District, a SFR development known as Linnen Place Subdivision, located off Hamlin Road. TMS No.: 578-00-00-049 through -050, 578-00-00-052, 578-00-00-477 through -501, 578-00-00-503, 578-00-00-506 through 578-00-00531, 578- 00-00-569 through -571

events.text:
Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachment 1).

Mr. Wren asked if this is similar to the Royal Palms annexation. Mr. Rutherford answered in the affirmative.

Ms. Smith asked if the disconnect between the county and Town zoning continues. Mr. Rutherford answered that this development was approved prior to the Sweetgrass Basket Overlay District (SB-OD) being established. Ms. Smith asked if this property could be included in the SB-OD. Mr. Rutherford answered that the request is to not be included in the SB-OD because it would mean the lots would be non-conforming.

Mr. Millet suggested that the coordination between the county and the Town should be a consideration during the Comprehensive Plan update. Planning Commission

Mr. Neal asked if the wetlands and open space would be owned by the homeowner’s association (HOA). Mr. Rutherford answered in the affirmative. Mr. Neal suggested that this is a good example of what occurs when zoning is denied and the property is developed in the county. Mr. Rutherford answered that the property could not previously be annexed as it was not contiguous to the Town.

Mr. Michael Churn, 2656 Lorne Drive, stated that they would like to annex into the Town and was the reason for requesting the annexation. He stated that the neighborhood would like to support the Town through being good citizens, voting, and paying taxes to the Town.

Mr. Shawn Smetana, 2631 Lorne Dr, stated that annexation was requested as they would like to vote in future Town elections. He asked if a crosswalk could be installed from their neighborhood to Hamlin Road for better pedestrian access to the school.

Ms. Leslie Wilke, 1288 Shingleback Dr, expressed concern with Billy Swails Blvd continuing next to their subdivision and asked if this could not occur.

There being no further comments, Mr. Wren closed the public hearing.

Ms. Campaigne asked for staff to respond to the previous comments. Mr. Rutherford stated that the Hamlin Road is a state road so the Town would need to coordinate with SCDOT. He stated that staff could work with the Transportation Department on these issues. He stated that the annexation is not needed to extend Billy Swails Blvd. Ms. Campaigne asked about the sidewalk. Mr. Rutherford answered that this would likely be in the existing SCDOT right-of-way and the Town would need their approval to install the sidewalk.

Ms. Gregg noted that this property is included in the Town planning area and would be included in the Comprehensive Plan update process.

Ms. Campaigne moved for approval including staff comments. Mr. McNeill seconded the motion. All in favor. Planning Commission

Mr. Ulma reviewed the request with the Committee (attachment 1).

Mr. Brimmer asked if the lot coverage would change from 40% to 50%. Mr. Ulma answered in the affirmative. Mr. Brimmer asked about drainage for this area. Mr. Mitchell answered that this is a concern because of the wetlands in proximity and is part of a larger watershed area. He stated that there are no issues with this subdivision. Mr. Brimmer asked if all the lots are developed. Mr. Ulma answered in the affirmative. Mr. Brimmer asked about Fulton 2 subdivision and if it has been built. Mr. Ulma answered in the negative.

Mr. O’Rourke asked about the five lots that were not being annexed. Mr. Rutherford answered that one owner was concerned with the possible extension of Fire Court, two owners were concerned with issues related to neighborhood political issues, and the other two owners were either out of the country or was not living on the property.

Mr. O’Rourke moved to recommend to Town Council approval of the request. Mr. Brimmer seconded the motion. All in favor. Planning Committee

providing for the annexation of an approximately 19.15 acre tract of land located near Hamlin Road identified by TMS Nos. 578-00-00-049 through -050, 578-00-00- 052, 578-00-00-477 through -501, 578-00-00-503, 578-00-00-506 through -531, 578-00-00-569 through -571 and depicted on plats recorded by the Charleston County ROD Office in Book L09, Page 0487-0488, Book L10, Page 0332-0333, and Book S12, Page 0161. (Ord. No. 18027) Mr. Bustos made a motion to approve the ordinance providing for the annexation of the 19.15 acre tract of land near Hamlin Road known as Linen Place; seconded by Mr. Brimmer. Michael Charen, 2656 Lohr Drive in Linen Place and represents the Board of Linen Place. He stated that they had approximately 90% of the homeowners who desired to annex into the Town of Mount Pleasant and be able to vote for Town Council and the Mayor. He said he has lived in Mount Pleasant for approximately 24 years and when he moved into Linen Place, he did not realize that he could not vote. He said they attempted annexation previously, but you must have an attachment, so now that they are, they look forward to being able to participate more in the Town. Mr. Santos asked why the other 10% did not want to annex into the Town. Mr. Charen stated that it was not 10, but 3 and they had some issues with two board members of Linen Place and does not believe it had to do with becoming part of the Town. He said that they definitely want to become part of the Town with the services involved. He said fire and rescue take a long time, when they could actually receive the service from the station at Six Mile.

Mr. Santos stated that he will be voting against this because historically he has always voted against the 75% method. He said that he does not like forcing anyone to annex into the Town. He said that he is happy they are coming into the Town but does not feel anyone should be forced. Mr. Santos was opposed. All other present voted in favor. Motion carries. Mr. DeMoura read FIRST READING BY TITLE ONLY. 5.

to zone R-4, Medium Density Residential District, an approximately 19.15 acre tract of land located near Hamlin Road, identified by TMS Nos. 578-00-00-049 through -050, 578-00-00-052, 578-00-00-477 through -501, 578- 00-00-503, 578-00-00-506 through -531, 578-00-00-569 through - 571 and depicted on plats recorded by the Charleston County ROD Office in Book L09, Page 0487-0488, Book L10, Page 0332-0333, and Book S12, Page 0161. (Ord. No. 18028) Mr. Bustos made a motion to approve the ordinance to zone R-4, the 19.15 acres known as Linen Place; seconded by Mr. Brimmer. Mr. Santos asked how this relates to the Town’s Comprehensive Plan and does it fit into the Comprehensive Plan. Mr. Ulma stated that the current Comprehensive Plan recommendation is for Community Conservation or Low Density; however, since it has already been developed under the County and developed before the Sweetgrass Basket Overlay, it does not fit the plan recommendations for that general area. Mr. Santos stated that it does not fit the Comprehensive Plan and does not fit the Sweetgrass Basket Overlay District. Mr. Ulma stated that this was approved by the County prior to much of the work and the ordinances being put in place, so effectively, it does not correspond because it was in advance of some of those requirements. He said the County did not impose the overlay either at the time.

Mr. Santos asked if it was currently in the Sweetgrass Basket Overlay District. Mr. Ulma stated that it is not included in the overlay, because it does not meet the requirements. Mr. Owens asked if any of the 19.15 acres, is undeveloped. Mr. Ulma stated that it is all developed except for the common area and they all include wetlands that were undeveloped parcels and cannot be further developed. All present voted in favor. Mr. DeMoura read FIRST READING BY TITLE ONLY. 6.

providing for the annexation of an approximately 19.15 acre tract of land located near Hamlin Road identified by TMS Nos. 578-00-00-049 through -050, 578-00-00- 052, 578-00-00-477 through -501, 578-00-00-503, 578-00-00-506 through -531, 578-00-00-569 through -571 and depicted on plats recorded by the Charleston County ROD Office in Book L09, Page 0487-0488, Book L10, Page 0332-0333, and Book S12, Page 0161. (Ord. No. 18027) [Mr. Bustos returned to the meeting at 7:40 p.m.] Mr. Ulma stated that this was done as a Planned Development District in the County and the annexation was accomplished through the process that allows the petition by the property owners. Ms. Whitley moved for approval; seconded by Mr. Bustos. Mayor asked if this development is built out. Mr. Ulma responded in the affirmative. Mr. Santos stated that when this was addressed previously, he was not in favor of the 75% method of annexation. He said there needs to be more clarity on the Council Agenda so the public understands that this is not a 100% annexation. He said 25% of the residents in this development are against annexing. He has never

been in favor of anything less than 100% annexation and will not be supporting this item. Mr. Bustos stated that he appreciates Mr. Santos’ stance; however, 100% is not required. He said he does not see any reason to tell everyone that it is not 100%, because it is not required. Mr. Santos stated that Mr. Bustos is making is sound like everyone agreed to annex; however, 25% of them did not agree. He does not feel this is right and as long as you are paying your taxes, you should be able to decide if you want to annex into a municipality or not. He said the public has a right to know when Council is making these decisions. Mr. Santos was opposed. All other present voted in favor. Motion to approve carries 8-1. Mr. DeMoura read FINAL READING BY TITLE ONLY. This Ordinance SIGNED, SEALED and DELIVERED this date. 4.

to zone R-4, Medium Density Residential District, an approximately 19.15 acre tract of land located near Hamlin Road, identified by TMS Nos. 578-00-00-049 through -050, 578-00-00-052, 578-00-00-477 through -501, 578- 00-00-503, 578-00-00-506 through -531, 578-00-00-569 through - 571 and depicted on plats recorded by the Charleston County ROD Office in Book L09, Page 0487-0488, Book L10, Page 0332-0333, and Book S12, Page 0161. (Ord. No. 18028) Ms. Whitley moved to approve; seconded by Mr. Bustos. All present voted in favor. Mr. DeMoura read FINAL READING BY TITLE ONLY. This Ordinance SIGNED, SEALED and DELIVERED this date. 5.

label: the corner of Penny Circle/Myrick Road
request: R-07-18 Rezone one parcel from R-1, Low Density Residential District, to R3, Medium Density Residential District, located at the corner of Penny Circle/Myrick Road (Avian Park). TMS No.: 532-08-00-028

events.text:
Mr. Wren recused himself due to a conflict of interest.

Ms. Canon reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2).

Mr. McNeill asked if Avian Park is zoned R-1. Ms. Canon answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Neal asked if the property is near the former mobile home park. Ms. Canon answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Brett Champion, reviewed the request with the Commission.

Mr. Lehman asked how it is proposed to be subdivided. Mr. Champion answered that it would be perpendicular with both lots having access from Myrick Road.

Ms. Campaigne asked if a variance was considered. Ms. Canon answered that there is no hardship to grant a variance.

Mr. Lehman asked if the surrounding lots are zoned R-1. Mr. Neal answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Thomas Dais, 1229 Myrick, suggested that the request is not in the best interest of the neighborhood. He suggested that this would set a precedent for the neighborhood and encourage more subdivisions in the area.

Mr. Brian Wurst, 1263 Myrick, expressed concern with the zoning request as the requested zoning could allow duplexes that would not be consistent with the character of the neighborhood. He suggested that this would be considered spot zoning. He suggested that this is a gateway property for the neighborhood. He suggested that there is no justification for the rezoning. Planning Commission

Ms. JoAnn Wurst, 1263 Myrick, suggested that this property has been vacant for many years, but has not seen a for sale sign on the property. She suggested that the neighborhood is zoned R-1 with ranch homes constructed on the lots. She suggested that the rezoning request would not be consistent with the neighborhood.

Mr. Neal closed the public hearing.

Mr. Champion suggested that the property would not allow duplexes. He stated that 21 of the 27 surrounding properties were in favor of the rezoning request. He suggested that this would be a good transition property for the lot.

Mr. Millet moved for denial of the request. Ms. Campaigne seconded the motion.

Ms. Smith suggested that the Commission should be vigilant with preserving the historic neighborhoods.

Mr. Neal agreed that the neighborhood character should be preserved.

Mr. McNeill agreed and suggested that it would set a bad precedent.

Ms. Gregg suggested that the public should participate in the rezoning process and voice their opinions. She suggested that the public should not “live in fear” of speaking out during meetings.

Mr. Neal called for a vote on the motion. All in favor with Mr. Wren abstaining.

Ms. Canon reviewed the request with the Committee (attachment 1).

Mr. O’Rourke asked if this could set a precedent for future subdivisions in the area that could potentially affect the character of the neighborhood. Ms. Canon answered that this was a concern from the neighborhood as well as the Planning Commission and the reason for denial of the request.

Mr. Brimmer agreed and stated that he had this concern as well when a neighboring parcel requested rezoning. He stated that he does not see that the rezoning would be of benefit to the Town.

Mr. Brimmer moved to recommend to Town Council denial of the request. Mr. O’Rourke seconded the motion. All in favor.

to rezone from R-1, Low Density Residential District to R-3, Medium Density Residential District, an approximately 0.33 acre tract of land located at the corner of Myrick Road and Penny Circle, described as Lot 13 in Avian Park Subdivision, identified by TMS No. 532-08-00-028, depicted on a plat recorded by the Charleston County ROD Office in Plat Book K, Page 151. (Ord. No. 18029) Mr. Santos moved for denial; seconded by Mr. Brimmer. All present voted in favor of denial. 7.

label: 1180 Freelock Drive
request: R-08-18 Rezone one parcel from R-1, Low Density Residential District, to OP, Office Professional District, located at 1180 Freelock Drive. TMS No.: 532-04-00-034

events.text:
Ms. Canon reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2).

Mr. Sal Parco and Ms. Andrea Parco, owner, reviewed the request with the Commission. Mr. Matthew Randall, civil engineer, reviewed the intended use Planning Commission

of the requested property for office space, employee parking, and approximately 14 additional spaces.

Mr. Millet asked if the existing home would be used for office space. Mr. Randall answered that if not rezoned to OP, then it would be used as a residence. Mr. Millet asked if the parking lot would be paved. Mr. Randall answered that low impact pervious material would be used.

Mr. Neal asked if the property would have access from Freelock Drive. Mr. Randall answered in the negative and stated that they would prefer to have access from Old Georgetown Rd.

Ms. Theresa Brailsford, 1181 Freelock Dr, stated that she lives across from the requested property. She expressed concern with a parking lot being located on the property and suggested that it would be out of character for the neighborhood. She stated that this is a well-established neighborhood with mature vegetation and plantings. She stated that Freelock Drive is a dead-end street and expressed concern with increased traffic. She asked that the neighborhood character be preserved. She stated that the increased traffic over the past couple of months has caused delay in garbage pickup and deliveries because of cars being parked along the street. She stated that she is opposed to the request.

Mr. Fred Auld, Freelock Dr, suggested that the requested property is the gateway to the neighborhood. He expressed concern with child and pedestrian safety. He stated that there are a lot of children in the area and expressed concern with the increased traffic in the area. He asked that the character of the neighborhood be preserved.

Mr. Robert Edens, 1167 Freelock Dr, suggested that the request would set a bad precedent for the neighborhood. He stated that he is opposed to the request.

Ms. Beth Lee, 1143 Freelock Dr, expressed concern with loss of property value and that this would set a bad precedent. She suggested that the request is a blatant disrespect for the existing neighborhood. She suggested that the request would be a detriment to the neighborhood. She stated that she is opposed to the request. Planning Commission

Mr. Mike Denson, 1020 Kip Lane, stated that parking is major issue in this area. He stated that the increased parking along the street is blocking traffic and deliveries. He expressed concern with a proposed parking lot on the property. He expressed concern with the request causing a decrease in property values. He stated that he is opposed to the request.

Mr. Tony Tronco, 1163 Freelock Dr, expressed concern with having a parking lot on the property as it would be in a residential neighborhood. He stated that he is opposed to the request.

Mr. Grayson King, 1151 Freelock Dr, expressed concern with the property being used for a parking lot. He stated that this request would set a precedent. He stated that he is opposed to the request.

Ms. Katy Quinn, 1155 Freelock Dr, expressed concern with safety. She expressed concern with child safety due to the increased traffic and parking on the right-of-way.

Ms. Christina Carl, 1104 Sea Island Crossing Lane, stated that she supports commercial along Chuck Dawley and Coleman Blvd and having restaurants near residential. She stated that based on the information presented, the restaurant has the required amount of parking. She stated that she is opposed to the request. She stated that the integrity of the neighborhood should be preserved. She suggested that the recent marking of the streets for allowed parking has been beneficial. She stated that the neighborhood is quiet and suggested that the parking lot would increase congestion and create “havoc”. She stated that the restaurant has recently re-opened and suggested that the increased traffic could be a temporary issue.

Ms. Kim Martin, 1139 Freelock Dr, stated that it is a quiet neighborhood and expressed concern that this would change the character of the neighborhood.

Mr. Shane Sinclair, 1174 Freelock Dr, expressed with the increased traffic and parking along Freelock. He suggested that the request could set a precedent for future more intensive commercial uses.

There being no further comments, Mr. Wren closed the public hearing. Planning Commission

Mr. Randall stated that they would like to be good neighbors and the reason for the additional parking is to alleviate the on-street parking along Freelock Dr. He suggested that a safer solution is needed to address the existing concern.

Mr. Neal suggested that this might not be the best solution. He asked if off-site parking has been considered. Mr. Randall answered in the affirmative and stated that it is difficult to control patrons parking along the street.

Mr. Millet moved for denial of the request. Mr. McNeill seconded the motion.

Ms. Smith suggested that it is not appropriate for the applicant to imply that if this request is not approved, then the parking would continue. She stated that this is an established residential neighborhood and suggested that the Commission should strive to preserve the established neighborhoods.

Mr. Neal suggested that this is the wrong solution for the issue. He commended the applicant for trying to determine a solution to the issue and suggested that the applicant should continue to look for other solutions. He suggested that rezoning the property to a commercial use is not the best option.

Ms. Campaigne commended the applicant for their businesses and their support of pedestrian and bike access. She agreed with the comment that business could only increase. She suggested that one solution would be to continue to encourage walking and biking to the restaurant.

Mr. Wren called for a vote on the motion. All in favor.

Mr. McNeill asked what the zoning is for the county property and suggested that a portion could be purchased and used as additional parking.

Ms. Canon reviewed the request with the Committee (attachment 1).

Mr. Brimmer asked if an office space would be constructed. Ms. Canon answered that the existing residence would be used as office space. Mr. Brimmer asked if there would be sufficient overflow parking. Ms. Canon answered that the applicant indicated that this could be accomplished, but if rezoned, the parking and any exterior renovations to the existing structure would require DRB approval.

Mr. Bustos suggested that this is not an appropriate use for the neighborhood.

Mr. O’Rourke moved to recommend to Town Council denial of the request. Mr. Brimmer seconded the motion. All in favor. Planning Committee

to rezone from R-1, Low Density Residential District, to OP, Office Professional District, an approximately 0.31 acre tract of land located at 1180 Freelock Drive, identified by TMS No. 532-04-00-034, depicted on a plat recorded by the Charleston County ROD Office in Plat Book S17, Page 0251. (Ord. No. 18030) Mr. Owens moved to deny; seconded by Mr. Brimmer. All present voted in favor of denial. 8.

label: 1236 Melvin Bennett Road
request: R-09-18 Rezone from R-1, Low Density Residential District, to AB, Areawide Business District, an approximately 1.00 acre tract of land comprised of one parcel in its entirety and portions of two parcels, located at 1236 Melvin Bennett Road. TMS No.: 560-02-00-038, 560-02-00-039 and 560-02-00-019 (portions thereof)

events.text:
Ms. Canon reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2). Planning Commission

Mr. Wren asked what the Commission vote was for the previous request for this property in January. Ms. Lynes stated that she would check the minutes. Mr. Wren asked if there is a survey or sketch plan delineating where the division of the property would occur. Ms. Canon answered that a rendering was included with the application but a sketch plan has not been submitted at this time.

Mr. McNeill asked the difference between AB and AB-2 zonings. Ms. Canon reviewed the differences between the zonings for the Commission.

Mr. Neal noted that the main difference between the zoning designations is the ability to have outdoor storage as a special exception.

Ms. Lynes answered that the Planning Commission recommended approval at the January meeting on a 7 to 2 vote.

Mr. Tim Askins reviewed the request with the Commission.

Mr. McNeill asked what the property would be utilized for. Mr. Askins answered that it would be used for a commercial office. Mr. McNeill answered that due to the size of the lot and the number of trees on the lot it would be difficult if zoned Office Professional (OP).

Mr. Neal asked if the request can be conditioned. Mr. Pagliarini answered in the negative. Mr. Neal asked if the property can be deed restricted. Mr. Pagliarini answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Wren asked if the deed restriction would be a civil matter. Mr. Pagliarini answered in the affirmative.

Mr. McNeill asked if the deed restriction could be removed. Mr. Pagliarini answered in the affirmative based on how the restriction is worded.

Mr. Shaun Rudy, 1228 Melvin Bennett, suggested that the property should remain residential. He expressed concern that there is no definite plan for the property. He suggested that more residential would be preferred to a commercial use. Planning Commission

Mr. John Burn, 1411 Breckon Road, stated that he owns the property adjacent to the requested property. He stated that Bowman Road is a well-traveled roadway and suggested that a residential use would not be preferred next to and adjacent to other commercial property. He suggested that the surrounding residents would not want additional traffic on Melvin Bennett. He suggested that this is a good opportunity and the request would be consistent with the surrounding uses.

Mr. Larry Heigg, Moss Park, expressed concern with the property being zoned commercial and that it would set a precedent and increase traffic along Melvin Bennett Road. He expressed concern with not knowing what uses would be on the property. He suggested that any proposed uses should be consistent with the surrounding neighborhood. He stated that he is opposed to the request.

There being no further comments, Mr. Wren closed the public hearing.

Mr. Askins stated that he has correspondence from the surrounding residents and distributed these to the Commission (attachment 3). He suggested that the deed restrictions would be done as a good faith effort and after consulting legal advice, would be done in perpetuity.

Mr. Wren asked if access would be from Melvin Bennett for the commercial portion. Mr. Askins answered in the negative and stated that the property would be separated by open space and buffers.

Mr. Neal asked if a buffer would be located between Mr. Rudy’s property. Mr. Askins answered in the affirmative and stated that he has been speaking with the owners about increasing the buffer in that area. Mr. Neal stated that the neighbors have expressed concern and suggested that an agreement should be secured if possible.

Mr. Lehman asked if Mr. Askins lives in the neighborhood. Mr. Askins answered in the negative.

Mr. Millet asked if any of the correspondence from the residents in favor of the request live on Melvin Bennett. Mr. Askins answered that some of the residents live across the street with their property fronting on Bluebird, but backs up to Melvin Bennett. Planning Commission

Ms. Gregg asked the reason for not requesting Neighborhood Commercial (NC). Mr. Askins answered that NC has a 6,000 square foot building maximum. Ms. Gregg asked if one reason for the request is to maximize parking. Mr. Askins answered that they prefer to construct one building at 7,500 square feet so that the parking is more accessible. Ms. Canon reviewed the different commercial zonings with the Commission. Ms. Gregg asked if there is a building maximum for OP. Ms. Canon answered in the negative. Mr. Askins answered that the difference would be the amount of parking required and the restriction of uses. He stated that AB zoning would allow more flexibility in uses allowed on the property.

Ms. Smith moved for denial of the request. Mr. Millet seconded the motion.

Ms. Smith suggested that this is considered spot zoning. She suggested that this issue should be considered through the Comprehensive Plan process.

Mr. Neal stated that Bowman Road is a growing transitional area. He suggested that residential was not appropriate for this parcel. He suggested that the Commission should decide based on the current Comprehensive Plan recommendation.

Mr. McNeill agreed that this is a difficult decision and suggested that residential on Bowman Road is not consistent with the area. He agreed that this is a transitional neighborhood. He agreed that there should not be spot zoning, but the Commission should look to the future and take into consideration the Comprehensive Plan recommendations.

Ms. Canon clarified that the request was not previously denied, but the request was withdrawn by the applicant.

Mr. Wren asked for clarification on spot zoning. Mr. Pagliarini answered that this would not be considered spot-zoning.

Ms. Gregg stated that this area was historically residential and became transitional with the placement of I-526. She stated that there are mobile homes located in the vicinity as well and suggested that these mobile homes could be considered affordable housing. Planning Commission

Mr. McNeill asked the zoning of the county property. Ms. Canon suggested that it was residential but did not have a definitive answer.

Mr. Wren called for a vote on the motion. Motion passed on a 7 to 1 vote with Ms. Campaigne, Ms. Gregg, Mr. McNeill, Ms. Smith, Mr. Lehman, Mr. Millet, and Mr. Neal in favor; Mr. Wren opposed.

There being no further business, the meeting adjourned at 7:26 pm.

Submitted by,

Ms. Canon reviewed the request with the Committee (attachment 1).

Ms. Mamie Rudy, 1232 Melvin Bennett, lives adjacent to the requested property and expressed concern with commercial property being adjacent to her back yard. She stated that this is a historical neighborhood and suggested that to keep the neighborhood character intact, the residential uses should be maintained for the entire property.

Mr. John Burn, 1411 Breckon Rd, lives across Bowman Road from the proposed property. He suggested that the request would be consistent with the commercial property along Bowman Rd.

Mr. Larry Haig, 1318 Bluebird Dr, suggested that if zoned commercial the commercial uses would further the “creep” along Melvin Bennett Road. He stated that another concern is that the type of commercial use is currently not known. He suggested that the property should remain residential.

Mr. Bustos asked if there is a bank located on the corner of Melvin Bennett. Ms. Canon answered in the affirmative.

Ms. Canon stated that the applicant submitted a rendering of the proposed office building and showed this for the Committee (attachment 1).

Mr. Tim Askins, applicant, stated that he has been working with the neighborhood to have a development that would be amenable to the neighborhood. He distributed a list of restriction of uses that would be included with the deed to the property. He stated that an eight-foot fence would be included around the commercial portion of the property. He suggested that this would be a separation of the neighborhood and not “creep”. He stated that he has coordination letters from Mount Pleasant Waterworks (MPW) and SCDOT. Planning Committee

Mr. Shaun Rudy, 1232 Melvin Bennett, stated that there is a residence on the commercial property on the corner of Chuck Dawley and Melvin Bennett. He expressed concern that this would be spot zoning and that the deed restriction would not prevent commercial uses in the future. He suggested that the request is not consistent with the neighborhood and that it should remain residential.

Mr. Bustos asked how many homes could be constructed if it remained residential. Ms. Canon answered that based on the acreage, five units could be constructed. Mr. Bustos suggested that having commercial uses on Bowman Road makes sense, with the remainder of the property along Melvin Bennett being residential as it would mean less impact. Mr. Bustos asked if the deed restriction would be upheld with a new owner. Mr. Pagliarini answered in the affirmative and stated that a change in the deed would be required if changes were desired.

Mr. O’Rourke asked if the fence would be constructed between the commercial portion and the residential property. Mr. Askins answered in the affirmative. Mr. Brimmer noted that the request cannot be conditioned. Ms. Canon agreed but noted that the commercial uses would require DRB approval.

Mr. O’Rourke moved to recommend to Town Council approval of the request. Mr. Bustos seconded the motion. All in favor.

Mr. Bustos stated that this is an error that was made that could be very costly to the neighborhood and their desires. to rezone from R-1, Low Density Residential District to AB, Areawide Business District, an approximately 1.00 acre tract of land comprised of one parcel in its entirety and portions of two parcels, described as follows: (i) an approximately 0.07 acre parcel in its entirety located on Melvin

Bennett Road, identified by TMS No. 560-02-00-038, depicted on a plat recorded by the Charleston County ROD Office in Plat Book CE, Page 190; (ii) an approximately 0.03 acre portion of an approximately 0.11 acre tract of land located on Melvin Bennett Road, identified by TMS No. 560-02-00-039, depicted on a plat recorded by the Charleston County ROD Office in Plat Book CE, Page 190; and (iii) an approximately 0.90 acre portion of an approximately 1.51 acre tract of land located at 1236 Melvin Bennett Road, identified by TMS No. 560-02-00-019, depicted on a plat recorded by the Charleston County ROD Office in Plat Book BA, Page 179. (Ord. No. 18031) Mr. Bustos moved for approval; seconded by Mr. Brimmer. Mr. Cunnane asked Mr. Ulma if there was discussion in terms of making this limited office instead of AB with staff. Mr. Ulma stated that he does not believe so. He said it began with AB-2 and then the request was to adjust it to AB. He said the third step to go to OP was not accomplished. He understands that the private deed restrictions were the mechanism they were looking at to narrow down the allowed uses on the property; however, there was not a request to alter it to OP. events.text:
Mr. Rutherford reviewed the staff report with the Commission. Planning Commission

Mr. Neal asked about if the two adjacent roads are town roads and fully constructed and does Lacannon connect to Hungryneck Blvd. Mr. Rutherford answered that the roads are county roads and Lacannon does not connect to Hungryneck Blvd. He stated that both roadways are not fully constructed.

Ms. Smith asked how the violation was determined. Mr. Rutherford answered that it was determined through a windshield survey of the property. Ms. Smith asked if there have been any neighborhood complaints. Mr. Rutherford answered in the negative. Ms. Smith asked how long the violation has occurred. Mr. Rutherford answered that based on aerial photos, it appears the violation has occurred for the past couple of years.

Mr. Millet asked if the construction business was located on the property when annexed. Ms. Canon answered that in reviewing the county tax records, it appears that there was an office use at the time of annexation. Mr. Millet asked when the HNB-VR-OD was established. Mr. Rutherford answered that it was established in 2006. Mr. Millet asked the reason for approval of the AB zoning. Mr. Rutherford answered that the AB zoning was consistent with the existing use of the property at that time. Mr. Millet asked what the underlying zoning is. Mr. Rutherford answered that it is AB.

Mr. McNeill asked what is located adjacent to the property. Mr. Rutherford answered that it is an orthodontist office. Mr. McNeill noted that there are commercial uses surrounding this property. He stated that a special exception would be needed from the Board of Zoning Appeals (BOZA) for the outdoor storage.

Ms. Smith asked about outdoor storage on some properties on the same road. Mr. Rutherford answered that the property is in the county.

Mr. Gates asked if the submittal should be accurate and are considered legal documents. Mr. Pagliarini answered that staff reviews the submittal to determine if the application is complete.

Mr. Greg St. Pierre, applicant, reviewed the request with the Commission. He stated that they are not opposed to remaining in the HNB-VR-OD. He stated that there have been no complaints from the neighbors on the current use of Planning Commission

the property. He stated that they are requesting the rezoning to bring the property into compliance.

Mr. Neal asked if the reason for the request is because of a code violation. Mr. St. Pierre answered in the affirmative. Mr. Neal asked if there is a privacy fence around the property. Mr. St. Pierre answered in the affirmative and stated that there is an eight-foot privacy fence with landscaping. Mr. Neal asked how the property is accessed. Mr. St. Pierre answered that there is access from Venning Road and Lacannon Lane. Mr. Neal asked if the access is paved. Mr. St. Pierre answered in the negative and stated that it is a gravel road.

Mr. Millet asked about the boat storage. Mr. St. Pierre answered that they allow boat storage in the overflow parking areas. Mr. Millet asked if they charge for the boat storage fee. Mr. St. Pierre answered in the negative.

Mr. Neal stated that he is supportive of the request as it would bring the property into compliance.

Mr. Millet asked about the removal from the HNB-VR-OD. Ms. Canon answered that staff explained the requirements of the HNB-VR-OD with the applicant prior to their submittal. She stated that because the request does not meet the intent of the HNB-VR-OD, staff recommended not including the property in the HNB- VR-OD; however, there is nothing in the overlay provisions that would prohibit the applicant from conducting the business as it is if it were to remain in the overlay.

There being no comments, Mr. Wren closed the public hearing.

Ms. Smith expressed concern with AB-2 as it would allow self-storage units. Mr. Rutherford answered that self-storage would require a conditional use approval.

Mr. Millet asked if there are restrictions on what type of storage is included in the special exception for the outdoor storage. Ms. Canon answered in the negative and stated that the special exception would be tied to a site plan and a specific use. Planning Commission

Mr. Wren asked if hotels are allowed in AB-2. Mr. Rutherford answered in the affirmative and stated that the overlay does restrict commercial building size to 15,000 square feet.

Mr. McNeill asked if a special exception and DRB approval would still be required. Mr. Rutherford answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Gates asked if the uses would be restricted according to the corporate documents and the uses allowed under the corporate documents. Mr. Pagliarini answered that the zoning would be approved for the property and not the specific user or owner. The zoning would dictate the types of uses allowed.

Mr. Millet moved for approval of the request. Mr. Neal seconded the motion.

Mr. Wren asked if the property should remain in the HNB-VR-OD.

Mr. Millet withdrew his motion. Mr. Neal withdrew his second.

Mr. Millet moved for approval of the rezoning request including all staff comments and denial of the request to remove the property from the HNB-VR- OD. Mr. Cuttino seconded the motion. All in favor.

Mr. Wren thanked staff for their work regarding code enforcement.

Action to be taken: Planning Commission recommended approval (9-0) BACKGROUND – SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES (SWF) ORDINANCE • “Small Wireless Facilities” (SWF) are intended to meet the demand for ever-increasing capacity, speed and reliability and are characterized as: • Aesthetically smaller designs • Improved user experience • Preference to attach to existing infrastructure • Platform for evolving technology • Small-Cell Wireless Facilities are geared to be located in in government right-of-ways (ROWs). • Requests to locate such facilities in Mount Pleasant have arisen, but our existing telecommunications ordinance does not directly address them. 28 BACKGROUND – SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES (SWF) ORDINANCE • In response to these changes, the industry worked with the Municipal Association of South Carolina (MASC) to create a model ordinance. • Staff prepared a reformatted version of this model ordinance to fit into Town ordinances, and then modified it to meet our community’s circumstances & needs. • After the required Public Hearing, Planning Commission recommended approval, 9-0. 29 BACKGROUND – SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES (SWF) ORDINANCE The proposed ordinance: • Was prepared by Planning and Legal staff & Supplements current Telecommunications Towers Ordinance • Establishes definitions, an application and review process, as well as design and development standards for SWF • Responds to some input & feedback received from one industry representative 30 OVERVIEW OF SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES (SWF) ORDINANCE • PURPOSE AND INTENT • APPLICABILITY • DEFINITIONS • APPLICATION PROCESS • FEES AND COSTS • APPLICATION REVIEW TIMEFRAMES AND TOLLING • CONSOLIDATED APPLICATION FOR MULTIPLE SWF 31 OVERVIEW OF SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES (SWF) ORDINANCE MAXIMUM HEIGHT

• In residentially zoned areas, maximum height can be same as existing street light pole or, if there is no street light pole, 40 feet tall. • In non-residentially zoned areas, maximum height can be 50 feet tall.

Existing light pole on Johnnie Dodds Blvd 32 OVERVIEW OF SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES (SWF) ORDINANCE APPEARANCE OF SWF IN COVERED AREAS • When there is no existing street light pole, the SWF must be the same or substantially similar in looks/materials to an approved light pole in a commercial corridor. • A proposed Wireless Facility cannot be any more visible than an existing utility structure, pole, or equipment located within 500 linear feet on the same Covered Area. • Where SWFs are determined to be appropriate, mitigation to avoid negative impacts may be required i.e. concealment treatment, control box, screening. 33 OVERVIEW OF SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES (SWF) ORDINANCE Examples from City and County of Denver’s Small Cell Infrastructure Design Guidelines. APPLICABLE DESIGN GUIDELINES Planning & Development Department will create Design Guidelines to maintain the quality of the surrounding area, with application approval dependent upon:  Location (any ground-mounted or wireless supported SWF) • Appearance and concealment (i.e. materials, screening, landscaping) • Design and appearance • Existing neighborhood covenants and restrictions 34 Acceptable Unacceptable OVERVIEW OF SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES (SWF) ORDINANCE Examples from City and County of Denver’s Small Cell Infrastructure Design Guidelines. APPLICABLE DESIGN GUIDELINES The Design Guidelines will give examples of SWF preferences including visual depictions.

Town has the authority to update the Design Guidelines with changes in law, technology, or administrative process.

If there is a conflict between the Design Guidelines and requirements in the Code of Ordinances, the Ordinance will take precedence over the Design Guidelines.

35 Acceptable Unacceptable OVERVIEW OF SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES (SWF) ORDINANCE HISTORIC AND DESIGN DISTRICTS • Must comply with all standards of that district to minimize negative impacts to the aesthetics and character of the district. The application will be denied if mitigation efforts (concealment, landscaping, material) are insufficient to the Town or the Board. • This section will not limit Town authority to enforce historic preservation zoning regulations.

36 OVERVIEW OF SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES (SWF) ORDINANCE GENERAL CONDITIONS AND REQUIREMENTS OF PERMIT APPROVAL

• SWF in ROWs will be a Permitted Use if it is in compliance with the standards in the Ordinance, Town Code, and all FCC, federal, state, and local laws.

• If any standards or regulations change, the Town is not required to give notice; however, the owners of the SWF must bring it up to compliance (within 90 days). If they do not, the SWF may be removed at the owner’s expense.

• The Town grants permits for a term of 6 months and reserves the right to conduct inspections with which the SWF owner must cooperate.

37 OVERVIEW OF SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES (SWF) ORDINANCE GENERAL CONDITIONS AND REQUIREMENTS OF PERMIT APPROVAL (CONTINUED)

• If a problem is identified with the SWF, the Town can take action to correct it at the owner’s expense (removal, relocation, adjustment).

• SWF permittee must keep accurate contact information for all associated parties (phone numbers, street mailing addresses, email addresses) and provide all information to the Planning Department.

• Good condition of SWF is required so general property maintenance is mandatory. Examples of poor condition include: peeling, flaking, or blistered paint; graffiti; rust or other visible deterioration; or failure to maintain any required landscape screening. 38 OVERVIEW OF SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES (SWF) ORDINANCE COVERED AREAS IN ANY ZONING DISTRICT IN WHICH OVERHEAD LINES HAVE BEEN PLACED UNDERGROUND

• The Town is currently placing certain overhead utility lines underground for aesthetic and enhanced service reasons so, in accordance with this effort, any wireless service provider must remove, relocate, or change the position of any SWF within the ROWs whenever the Town deems it necessary.

• If this is necessary, the Town will give the wireless service provider written notice. The provider has 90 days following the notice to comply.

39 OVERVIEW OF SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES (SWF) ORDINANCE LEGAL ENTITY REMOVAL OF SWF IF USE DISCONTINUED OR ABANDONED If a SWF owner does not notify the Town of discontinued use or abandonment after 90 days, it will be considered abandoned and can be removed at the owners expense.
