events.text:
Mr. Wren stated that the applicant has requested a deferral of this request. Letter Requesting Deferral Planning Commission Agenda

Mr. Neal moved for approval of the request to defer this request. Ms. Smith seconded them motion.

Mr. Pagliarini clarified that there was a clerical error and misunderstanding regarding this request. He stated that since this is a mutual misunderstanding and the public hearing is not being opened for this item, so the request would not be considered a denial and could be deferred.

Mr. Wren called for a vote on the motion. All in favor.

Ms. Reed reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachment 1). Planning Commission

Mr. Jonathan Yates, Mr. Nick Wyndham, Mr. Murphy Duffy, and Mr. Jody McInerny reviewed the request with the Commission.

Ms. Linda Seaton, 561 Galero Lane, suggested that the Commission is elected and that this should be reconsidered if the desires of the citizens are not heard for this request. She recited names of experts in cell service, NSA, UN, etc. She suggested that these individuals are experts on 5G and that this request is in direct response to the recent technology.

Mr. Rob Turquoise, attorney with Rice Motley, stated that cell towers have non-ionized radiation and early studies did not provide sufficient information on the effects of cell tower radiation on health. He stated that studies within the last ten years indicate that the radiation causes significant health issues.

Mr. Bob Hamis, Longpoint resident, stated that he is opposed to the request. He expressed concern with child health issues associated with cell towers. He asked that this radiation be kept from the children and residents.

Ms. Amy McCloud, 125 King St, stated that it is the FCC that regulates cell towers and does not prohibit decisions made based on health concerns. She expressed concern with decrease in property values. She expressed concern that the cell tower would cause health issues for the surrounding residents.

Ms. Michele DeMarco, 1854 Peaceful Way, expressed similar concerns with the cell tower that have already been addressed. She questioned whether the Longpoint residents were surveyed on what kind of service they currently receive.

Mr. Nathan Bowers, 192 Oak Landing Drive, expressed concern with child safety and the unknown of the effects the cell tower may have. He suggested that the reason for the proposed location was to be farther away from residents because of the effects of the cell tower, the affect to property values, and that it is unsightly.

Mr. Matt Everson, 324 Wild Horse Lane, suggested that there is a decrease of Verizon coverage at his home. He stated that access to first responders is important as well as being able to contact family members. He expressed Planning Commission

concern with decrease in property values due to poor service in the area. He stated that he has started a petition allow the cell tower.

Ms. Cindy Campson, 794 Needlerush Parkway, asked how the request met the waiver criteria. She suggested that there are other neighborhoods that would be impacted by the cell tower that were not heard.

Mr. Brian Wilson, 1976 Long Circle, suggested that there was not a proper vote from the POA for approval of the cell tower.

Mr. Mark Angelino, 926 Richter Way, suggested that more information is needed and more questions should be asked by the Commission to have a clear understanding of what is involved with providing cell service in regard to purported health issues.

Mr. Brett Hamis, 395 Palmetto Bluff, suggested that Lloyds of London will not insure a cell tower because of the potential liability. He suggested that more research should be done before a decision is made on this request. He expressed concern with child safety.

Ms. Sara Purcell, James Island, suggested that 5G is damaging to human health and areas around the world are banning this type of service because of the potential health issues.

Mr. Cao Yong, 1939 Enclave, stated that their subdivision was not aware of this request. He expressed concern with child safety and has done some research regarding potential health dangers associated with cell towers.

Mr. James Tweedy, 1938 Tyson Lane, expressed concern with child safety and the proximity of the cell tower to recreation facilities. He suggested that the HOA Board of Directors approved the lease of the cell tower without permission from the residents. He asked that this not be approved.

Ms. Karen Gadol, 2558 Kingsfield, stated that as a physician that treats cancer patients, she is aware of the potential exposure to radiation of cell towers. She suggested that this should be considered in making a decision. Planning Commission

Mr. Joan Warlock, 184 Oak Point Landing, expressed concern with the health hazards associated to cell towers. She also expressed concern that the residents did not provide input on the cell tower.

Mr. Ty Curtis, 316 Springhill Lane, stated that he was not aware of the request until today and was not aware of the lease being approved by the HOA.

Mr. Rick O’Lair, 2033 Arundel, expressed concern with the proximity of the cell tower to the recreation facilities and child safety. He suggested that more information on the possible effects of 5G should be provided.

Ms. Melissa Endal, 4009 Crowne Pointe, expressed concern with the proximity of the cell tower to recreation facilities and where children play. She suggested that a more logical location should be determined.

There being no further comments, Ms. Smith closed public comment.

Ms. Smith moved for denial. Mr. Gates seconded the motion. Motion passed on a 5 to 1 vote, with Mr. Bennett, Mr. Davis, Mr. Gates, Ms. Smith, and Mr. McCormick in favor; Mr. Campbell opposed.

Amendment proposes repealing Exhibit B and replacing it with new Exhibit showing new location for Access “F.” (Ord. No. 22017) January 19, 2022 Planning Commission Meeting Minutes January 31, 2022 Planning Committee Meeting Minutes Ms. Whitley moved for final reading, seconded by Mr. Iacofano. Mr. Chapman said there is a plan for access into the property from the rear, and that was part of the plan as it was developed for the entire Carolina Park project. He stated the developer planning this in their present location continues to have vehicles parked in the buffer zone as late as this weekend, and extensively. He would like to ask if it is possible to have a clause for this amendment if they do the same thing on this site where they are parking vehicles in the buffer zone. He asked if it is possible to do this to force them to keep the vehicles out of the buffer zone. Ms. Reed said the reason this was not on the consent agenda is because Mr. Chapman stated he would like to make some amendments such as no parking in the buffer and no future plans for a left turn where the median is located. She stated because it is a planned development amendment, we could attach those conditions, and asked Mr. Pagliarini to confirm. Mr. Pagliarini stated that is correct. Mr. Chapman moved to add those two amendments to make sure we do not get left turns in or out, and to require no parking in the buffer zone, and if they do park there, that entrance closes. Mayor Haynie asked if no parking in the buffer zone is already covered by an ordinance, and perhaps it is just an enforcement issue. Ms. Reed said if they violate this condition or this zoning provision, she does not know if that would change anything in the approved planned development. She said it would be a code enforcement issue. Mr. Pagliarini stated the Town would have the right to enforce within the context of the planned development so he feels it is relevant if Mr. Chapman would like to include it. Mr. Chapman moved to amend the ordinance so that in the future, no left turns would be made in or out of this development at location F, and second, in the event we have the same problem in the current location, that the direct access to 17 be closed. Mayor asked for clarification if Mr. Chapman was referring to the right turn in, and Mr. Chapman concurred. Mr. Chapman said enforcement had a very difficult time trying to get the vehicles out of the buffer area, and he is putting this in here because they worked for over two years to try and get the vehicles out of there. He said other dealerships were staying outside the buffer so there is no reason for this. Ms. Whitley seconded the motion. Mr. Pagliarini stated for clarification that we cannot close access for a violation. Mayor Haynie said that would affect the second part of Mr. Chapmans amendment and asked Mr. Chapman if he would like to strike that part. Mr. Chapman amended his motion to strike the closing of the access for violations. Ms. Whitley amended her second. After further discussion, Mayor Haynie called for the vote on the amendment and Mayor Haynie, Mr. Chapman, Ms. Hyatt, Mr. Ritchie and Ms. Whitley voted in favor with Ms. Corley, Mr. Santos, Mr. Rambo and Mr. Iacofano voting opposed. The motion for the amendment carried with a 5-4 vote. Mayor Haynie called for the vote on final reading of the amended ordinance and all present voted in favor. This Ordinance SIGNED, SEALED and DELIVERED this date

events.text:
TMS no. 532-03-00-022 is currently zoned R-1 Low Density Residential, requesting to rezone to R-3 Medium Density Residential. Mr. Stone reviewed staff comments with the Commission.

Ms. Kelsey Santiago and Mr. Buzzy Branbill, reviewed the request with the Commission.

Ms. Kate Womble, 1037 North Shem Drive, stated that she and many of her neighbors are opposed to the request. She expressed concern that the rezoning would mean smaller lots, more density, and more traffic. She suggested that if approved, this request would mean an approximate 50% increase in density. She expressed concern with pedestrian and child safety, drainage, and flooding. She asked that the current zoning remain to preserve the neighborhood.

Ms. Angela Burchfield, 942 South Shem, expressed opposition to the rezoning and asked that the request be denied. She stated that many in her neighborhood are opposed to the rezoning as it would increase density. She stated that there is a petition signed by the residents in opposition of the request and asked that the residents’ request be upheld.

Mr. Frank Toler, 949 South Shem, expressed opposition to the rezoning request. He suggested that the current zoning should remain. He suggested that the rezoning request is in opposition of the Comprehensive Plan. He also expressed concern with drainage and that this project would exacerbate the issue.

Ms. Kara Campbell, 955 South Shem, expressed concern with drainage and asked that the request be denied.

Mr. Mike McCullough, 1125 Sea Island Crossing Way, stated that he is opposed to the request. He expressed concern with pedestrian and child safety. He suggested that the project would increase traffic and endanger the children. He suggested that improvements are needed before additional Planning Commission

development is approved in addition to the sidewalks being connected for the area. He asked the Commission to deny the request.

Ms. Patricia Blair, 1166 BB Lane, expressed concern with the request. She stated that she is opposed to the request. She expressed concern that the request would increase traffic and cause additional vehicular accidents. She expressed concern with child safety. She suggested that BB Lane is a private road, and that this development would be detrimental to her property and her quality of life.

Ms. Kim Berkheimer, 1182 Russell Drive, stated that BB Lane is a private roadway. She suggested that if the request is approved, there is not sufficient infrastructure to support the development and it would increase traffic for the area.

Mr. David Bedair, 1156 Russell Drive, Lot 23, asked that the request be denied. He suggested that there is already significant traffic in the area and would increase with the development. He expressed concern with drainage and suggested that development would increase the drainage issues in the area. He asked that the project be denied.

Mr. Joe Bustos, 649 King Street, agreed that the residents have been well spoken. He stated that he supports the requests from the neighborhood for denial of the request. He expressed concern with increasing traffic in the area.

Mr. Reese Artigues, 1047 Governor Road, stated that the property is currently zoned to allow up to 40 homes. He stated that the proposal is to reduce the number of homes to 20 homes. He suggested that the main cause of traffic is the nearby school and is only during the morning and afternoon school days. He suggested that he has met with the applicant and the applicant expressed a desire to meet with the school to review the project. He stated that he supports the request.

There being no further comments, Mr. Wren closed public hearing.

Ms. Santiago noted that the number of homes would be significantly reduced. She stated that they are willing to work with the staff to meet the drainage and tree requirements and have already started discussion. She Planning Commission

stated that they are also working with MPW regarding water and sewer. She stated that they understand the historic tree issue and stated that they want to preserve the trees on the property as much as possible.

Ms. Smith moved for denial of the request. Mr. Davis seconded the motion.

Ms. Smith suggested that this is an infill project. She suggested that there is an obligation to the existing neighborhoods to protect them from increased density. She also noted that there are drainage issues in the area that should be addressed as well before more development is approved. She suggested that the current zoning should remain.

Mr. Davis suggested that the project would cause “overdevelopment” of the property and agrees with Ms. Smith’s comments.

Mr. Wren agreed that the requested zoning is not compatible with the neighborhood.

Mr. Wren called for a vote on the motion. All in favor.

Ms. Reed reviewed the agenda item with the Committee Mr. Chapman shared that the entrance of Christ our King school and church is heavily trafficked. Ms. Hyatt asked about the setbacks. Ms. Corley moved to deny the request. Ms. Hyatt seconded the motion. All present voted in favor of denial.

F.Proposal to amend Sections 156.340 - 156.345 of Chapter 156, Zoning Code, of the Mount Pleasant Code of Ordinances, pertaining to Short Term Rentals. Proposed is to amend the entire ordinance to clean up outdated language, and to the clarify language related to the cap and how it is administered based on those already operating a STR. On June 6th Planning Committee reviewed the extents of this proposal and motioned that it be remanded back to the Planning Commission for input.

Ms. Reed reviewed staff comments with the Commission.

Ms. Smith suggested that there should be a distinction between renters at the 4% tax rate and those at 6% rate. She also suggested that the permit fees should be increased. She stated that the number of days showing use of the STR permit could coincide with the state threshold that triggers the increase to the 6% tax rate.

Mr. Bennett suggested approval of the draft with staff determining some minimum standards, delaying a vote and have staff come back with changes, or making a recommendation of changes.

Mr. Gates asked the average daily rental is for a short-term rental and suggested that the fees should be increased. Ms. Reed stated that the average daily rate for a short-term rental is $230 per night. She also reviewed the proposed total revenue from all short-term rentals.

The Commission agreed and recommended the following changes to the short-term rental program: ØAllow for two types of permits—one for those operating at the 4% tax rate and one for those operating at a 6% tax rate. ØIncrease the permit application fee to $1,500, particularly for those properties being assessed at a 6% tax rate. ØThere should be a minimum number of nights of use for 4% properties of 28 days; 72 days for 6% properties ØIncrease number of permits allowed to 450, particularly if moving to two separate permits ØClean up definition of terms for consistency such as owner versus operator, principal dwelling versus principal structure, local designated agent versus local emergency contact, etc. G.Presentation by Engineering and Development Services staff, detailing the Land Development approval process, as administered by the Development Review Team. Presentation will cover purview of both Town staff and Planning Commission in vesting Sketch Plans.

Ms. Smith moved for deferral to the next months meeting. Ms. Ireland seconded the motion. All in favor.

and open space requirements. Reed estimated approximately 130 residential units could be built by-right without triggering an impact assessment, along with 40,000 square feet of commercial. He expressed frustration that despite council being accused of shutting Belk's down and shutting down the movie theater, which couldn't be further from the truth, they must still address the situation. He noted Planning Commission had recommended approval with conditions including: height limited to 55 feet on exterior, 60,000 square feet dedicated to family entertainment if Regal closes, 14% green space (up from 10% shown), 6 market rate to 2 attainable housing units ratio, and 2 designated incubator locations. Iacofano recognized the developer had made many requested changes over 4 years but concluded there's still work to be done. Councilmember Hyatt stated the item came before council without committee recommendation due to unforeseen circumstances and the applicant's request. She objected to just a request for entitlements without a plan, emphasizing once we do that, it doesn't come back to us. It is out of our hands. He stated that SCDNR is currently not in any negotiations with the other stakeholders of this project. Ms. Susan Porter stated that SCDNR agreed to swap 4.69 acres with Patriots Point for a drainage ditch, parking, and the Vietnam display. In exchange, the easement was extended to 2048. She expressed concern that this project would not be an enhancement or preservation of the easement, but would destroy the habitat and negatively impact the migratory birds and butterflies. events.text:

Mr. Ferrara left at this time (5:55 pm). Ms. Sanford left at this time (5:57 pm).

Ms. Tori Sanders, Coastal Conservation League, expressed concern with the environmental implications of the proposed plan, particularly moving the grand lawn to the rear of the buildings rather than closer to the waterfront as it reduces the connectivity to the waterfront. She expressed concern that having the open space closer to the waterfront provides crucial ecosystem support and allows for better stormwater infiltration, reduces runoff, and protects water quality in the harbor and marsh. She suggested that it is a critical area for wildlife, provides bio-diversity, and provides a better cohesive ecological and environmental asset. She expressed concern with having large parking areas near the water and suggested that multi-modal uses and other parking strategies should be considered. Planning Commission

Ms. Katie Zimmerman, Executive Director for Charleston Moves, thanked the applicant for inclusion of bike and pedestrian access and suggested that conversations for further connectivity for those biking, walking, and using transit should be considered as it is important for the community. She suggested that more detailed streetscapes, trailscapes, and connections to those resources as the project moves forward.

Mr. Ian Duncan, 1427 Topaz, stated that reason for moving the grand lawn was to allow for a more active waterfront village. He also noted that the property naturally drains toward the golf course.

Mr. David Quick 1502 Village Square, suggested that there is an opportunity for more green space, as well as biking and pedestrian connectivity. He stated that he is comfortable with the new layout with the open space relocated. He suggested that an elevated waterfront walkway should be considered and brought to fruition. He suggested that native plantings should be considered during landscaping.

Ms. Michele Stress, 545 Veranda View, agreed that this project is a great opportunity to showcase different environmental designs and green technologies that would better preserve the natural spaces, wildlife, and native trees within the Town.

Mr. Wilson rebutted that the parking would be based on the ULI regulations. He stated that the PD includes a plan that would exceed the minimum of 10% open space required. He stated that the PD language would include the requirements within the current WG-OD. He stated that they would like to have the walkway continue along the entire waterfront.

There being no further comments, Mr. Lacy closed public comment.

Ms. Ireland moved for approval of the PD and conceptual plan with the following conditions: ➢ A broader visual corridor of green space from the hotel to the waterfront, which will necessitate minimizing the mixed-use buildings at waterfront; ➢ Prohibit residential uses on the ground floor with the residential use Planning Commission

ratio consistent with the current code of four residential units per acre with allowing an additional four units per acre if those additional units are for attainable housing; ➢ Maximize boardwalk and walkways for maximum connectivity for biking, pedestrian, and other access; ➢ Under the building design elements, change the use of stucco to be used as a secondary material, minimize the use of flat roofs, but if flat roofs are utilized, they should be green roofs; ➢ To the extent possible add an additional retention pond on right near the parking for additional open space. Mr. Lacy seconded the motion.

Mr. Lacy moved to amend the motion to remove the condition of minimizing the use of flat roofs and that they should be green roofs. Motion failed due to the lack of a second.

Mr. Tinkey moved to amend the motion to add the condition to require a 40% tree canopy for the site utilizing native trees including living oaks. Ms. Ireland seconded the amendment. All in favor.

events.text:
Mr. Stone reviewed staff comments with the Commission.

Mr. Tim Cook, property owner and civil engineer, reviewed the request with the Commission.

Ms. Claudia Page, 2007 Welsh Pony, expressed concern that there is only one way in and out of the neighborhood. She also expressed concern with the amount of traffic that currently exists and that this proposed development could increase traffic. She asked that there not be access from the commercial properties to the residential portion of the neighborhood.

Mr. Paul Barattini, 1162 Triple Crown Court, suggested that a 1,000-foot separation between the residences and the proposed development is not a Planning Commission

long distance. He suggested that there should not be connectivity to the residences. He expressed concern with the actual activities that could be associated with the flex space.

Ms. Theresa Rowland, 2023 Welsh Pony, expressed concern with the proposed location and asked that there be a condition restricting the development from being moved from the proposed location. She expressed concern with the berm and fence and suggested that this should be installed regardless of what or where this proposed development is located. She suggested that many of the homes are smaller in height than previously stated.

Mr. John Nunes, 1211 Banker Court, suggested that if the berm is not constructed, the fence should then be twelve feet. He suggested that the location of the proposed development should be restricted to this location. He suggested that all conditions and stipulations should be in writing to ensure they are carried out and enforced.

Mr. Mark Berry, 2012 Welsh Pony Drive, agreed with all previous comments. He suggested that there should be a wall constructed to help better screen the noise. He suggested that the 1,000-foot separation does not lessen the amount of noise. He also suggested that the wall should be taller to help prevent noise spill over to the residential units.

Ms. Bobbie Grogan, 2011 Welsh Pony, suggested that there should be a dedicated ingress/egress to the commercial development. She suggested that if a dedicated ingress/egress cannot be accomplished, then some other traffic flow solution such as a roundabout at the entrance to help reduce traffic into the residential area. She suggested that the widening the buffer behind the residential area should be considered to better separate the commercial area from the residential and help with noise. She questions whether another storage unit is needed and if the HOA could sufficiently enforce regulations.

Mr. Robert Waterfield, 2044 Welsh Pony, suggested that a flex space should be restricted. He expressed concern with traffic and that this proposed development would increase traffic in the area on an already congested roadway. He suggested that signalization and a reduction of the speed limit should be considered for better safety. Planning Commission

Mr. Steven Catalano, 3847 Tupelo Church Lane, expressed concern with traffic and noise. He that there is a way to have a balance between the commercial development and the residential portion of the neighborhood by having specific restrictions set forth in writing. He suggested that access for the commercial development should be restricted, with dedicated entrances, and a wall constructed to help screen noise. He suggested that the flex space should be clearly defined in the PD, including the location and design requirements to avoid any confusion in the future.

Mr. John Rowland, 2023 Welsh Pony, suggested that there should be more of a buffer between the commercial and residential uses. He suggested a master plan should be determined so there is a better understanding of future development in the area.

Mr. Josh Cheney, 3964 Hanoverian, expressed appreciation for the developer agreeing to build the wall for better noise suppression. He expressed concern with potential adverse effects on the wetlands. He suggested that the limits mentioned by the developer should be included in the PD.

There being no further comments, Mr. Bennett closed the public hearing.

Mr. Ferrara moved for approval of the planned development (PD) with the indoor flex space to be located at the top right quadrant and not moved more than 5% from proposed location as represented in the conceptual plan presented, the buffer wall to be studied and for the developer to work with staff for a height to be 10 feet-12 feet; total height of flex space to be no more than 35 feet; and no removal of trees behind Welsh Pony. Mr. Smyth seconded the motion.

Ms. Ireland moved to amend the motion to include elimination of the outdoor storage provision and to eliminate the hospice and substance abuse uses. Mr. Smyth seconded the motion. Amendment passed on an 8 to 1 vote with Mr. Ferrara, Mr. Smyth, Mr. Bennett, Ms. Sanford, Mr. Lacy, Ms. Mansour, Mr. Tinkey and Ms. Ireland in favor; Mr. Davis opposed. Planning Commission

Mr. Bennett called for a vote on the motion as amended. Motion passed on an 8 to 1 vote with Mr. Ferrara, Mr. Smyth, Mr. Bennett, Ms. Sanford, Mr. Lacy, Ms. Mansour, Mr. Tinkey and Ms. Ireland in favor; Mr. Davis opposed.

Ms. Ireland moved for approval of the impact assessment. Mr. Ferrara seconded the motion. Motion passed on an 8 to 1 vote with Mr. Ferrara, Mr. Smyth, Mr. Bennett, Ms. Sanford, Mr. Lacy, Ms. Mansour, Mr. Tinkey and Ms. Ireland in favor; Mr. Davis opposed.

Ms. Mansour moved for approval of the conceptual plan. Ms. Ireland seconded the motion. Motion passed on an 8 to 1 vote with Mr. Ferrara, Mr. Smyth, Mr. Bennett, Ms. Sanford, Mr. Lacy, Ms. Mansour, Mr. Tinkey and Ms. Ireland in favor; Mr. Davis opposed.

Mr. Rambo moved to recommend to Town Council approval of the request. Mr. Chapman seconded the motion.

Mr. Rambo moved to amend the motion to include the requirement for a 35-foot buffer with an eight-foot masonry wall between the residential units and the commercial site instead of a berm. Mr. Chapman seconded the amendment.

(Ord. 25026) April 23, 2025 Planning Commission Minutes May 5, 2025 Planning Committee Minutes Ms. Reed presented the request to incorporate a 1-acre tract of land into the Watermark Planned Development. The property, currently zoned AB (Areawide Business), fronts Bowman Road just off Chuck Dawley Boulevard. The applicant wanted to allow for car rental with outdoor display/storage of rental vehicles. Rather than rezoning to AB-2, which would allow more intense uses, the applicant proposed to join the Planned Development with limited conditions allowing just the car rental use. The Planning Commission had recommended approval with an enhanced buffer—a full 25-foot buffer with an 8-foot masonry wall— along the residential portion of the property line. The Planning Committee made no recommendation. A motion to deny was made by Councilwoman Hyatt and seconded by Councilman Chapman. During discussion, Councilman Rambo noted that the property would be developed regardless, and the current proposal with enhanced buffers would be less intensive than many other allowed uses under the current zoning. Councilwoman Hyatt expressed concerns about deed restrictions that had been promised when the property was originally rezoned from R-1 to AB-1, which appeared to prohibit vehicle rental with outdoor storage.

Mr. Pagliarini clarified that the town could not enforce private deed restrictions, though residents could seek enforcement through civil courts. Mayor Haynie called for a vote and the motion to deny failed with a 4-4 vote. Councilwoman Hyatt and Councilmen Chapman, Iacofano and Santos voted in favor of denial, with Councilmen Brownstein, Rambo, Tinkey and Mayor Haynie voting opposed. (2)

providing for the annexation of an approximately 0.93-acre parcel located at 1490 Boston Grill Road, depicted on a plat recorded by the Charleston County ROD Office in Plat Book BE, Page 27. (Ord. No. 26002) Planning Committee recommended denial.

Town Council Meeting Town Council Meeting Ms. Reed presented the next two items explaining that these ordinances would annex and zone a 0.93-acre parcel on Boston Grill Road. She noted that the property is located within the Hamlin Beach historic designation and would be zoned as CC (Community Conservation). The Planning Committee had recommended denial of the annexation, but

Town Council Meeting should it be annexed, both the Planning Commission and Committee recommended the CC zoning. During discussion, Council Member Tinkey expressed concerns about annexing properties from historic communities, noting that areas like Brickyard, Seaside, and the Old Village have protective overlays that prevent such actions. He emphasized that these historic settlements dating from after the Civil War deserve similar protections and mentioned that the town has been working for three years on establishing equivalent historic overlays. Council Member Rambo disagreed with this perspective, arguing that denying annexation would not prevent development. He explained that if annexation is denied, Mount Pleasant Water Works would still have to provide water and sewer by law, allowing development to proceed without town impact fees or taxes. He questioned the argument that these communities should have protection similar to HOA neighborhoods, pointing out that not all neighborhoods have HOAs and not all property owners want to be included in historic overlays. Ms. Reed clarified that three settlement communities east of the Cooper (Hamlin Beach, 10 Mile, and Phillips) already have historic designations in the county. She explained that 10 Mile Community recently completed work to draft and adopt a zoning overlay, and that Hamlin Beach would be the next community to develop such protections, followed by Phillips. She noted that town staff are working to determine how the town could adopt the same historic overlay and whether that might involve creating a joint commission. After further discussion about the timing of potential historic overlay protections, the Mayor indicated he would vote with the Planning Committee's recommendation to deny the annexation. A roll call vote was conducted on the motion to approve the annexation. Motion to approve the ordinance was made by Council Member Rambo and seconded by Council Member Chapman. Council Members Brownstein, Whitaker, Chapman, Hyatt, Rambo and Iacofano voted in favor with Council Members Crosby, Tinkey and Mayor Haynie voting opposed. The motion carried with a 6-3 vote. (3)

to rezone from OP-2 Office Professional-2 District to R-3, Residential District, two parcels located on the corner of White Flat and Bowman Road, consisting of approximately 0.47 acres in aggregate as indicated in Charleston County Plat Book BU, Page 130, and Book EB, Page 333. (Ord. No. 26016) Planning Commission recommended approval; Planning Committee recommended denial. Ms. Reed presented the request pertaining to two properties at the corner of Bowman and White Flat Road, currently zoned OP2 office professional. She provided history that before 2019 they were zoned R1 historically. The structure was constructed without proper permits as a commercial building, and to make it right, town staff and council worked with the previous owner and rezoned to office professional. There were further issues with the building regarding parking, buffers, and meeting commercial codes, so it sat vacant since that time and changed ownership. The current request was to zone it back residential, but instead of R1, the request was for R3. These were two separate parcels under same ownership. R3 would allow duplex dwelling and single-family detached, while R1 only allowed single-family detached. In light of a text amendment later on the agenda dealing with density, these parcels would only be eligible based on square footage for single-family detached for each one, but R3 was more appropriate given property sizes - one was 11,000 square feet (suitable for R1), the other 9,000 (more like R2), but they could have single-family or duplex under R3, though based on size they were likely only to get one unit on each lot. Council Member Chapman noted this parcel had been an issue for quite some time, going back to when he was on the Planning Commission years ago, and they were no better off today than then. He thought that was reason to deny and put this in conjunction with others in the neighborhood to help protect it. Ms. Reed mentioned that when speaking with residents living behind there, they would like it to remain R1. Since it fronted Bowman Road, they were opposed to R3 density at the front of their neighborhood. Council Member Brownstein asked about the applicant's earlier comment that you could not fit an R1 lot on those properties. Ms. Reed explained these were legally established lots that were historically zoned R1. If the owner came in to subdivide, that would be an issue, but these lots had been in place and could likely get building permits. The larger one at 11,000 square feet met R1 requirements of 10,000 square feet. The smaller at 9,000 would not quite meet the threshold but could get certain variances from setbacks as a nonconforming lot. Council Member Rambo asked about the comprehensive plan and future land use. These were designated mixed neighborhood, which allowed R1, R2, R3, R4, townhouse, or multifamily, so any would be appropriate. Council Member Hyatt confirmed they were currently office professional and asked if they could do mixed use like office with apartment upstairs. Ms. Reed said the problem with the current building was trying to have commercial use and meet parking and buffers. Originally, they were approved because they purchased a lot across the street for parking, but they went to the board of zoning appeals in 2023 to get variances from parking, buffers, and setbacks, and were denied. Ms. Reed said perhaps if they demolished the building and put a much smaller building depending on use, they could meet requirements. Council Member Hyatt moved for denial, seconded by Council Member Chapman. All present voted in favor. (4.)

providing for an amendment to the Johnson Tract Development PD-MU-SU (Ordinance No. 14084, as amended), also known as Indigo Square by permitting Drive-Thru uses on an approximately 1.10-acre parcel located at the corner of Highway 17 North and Indigo Market Drive. (Ord. No. 26020) Planning Commission recommended approval; Planning Committee recommended approval. Council Member Whitaker moved for approval, seconded by Council Member Crosby. Ms. Reed explained this was an amendment to the Indigo Square planned development district ordinance. Several years ago in 2023, this was all one property owned by Olive Branch AME Church zoned R1. They zoned the church property PI1 and broke off a parcel just over an acre, incorporating it into the PD. It was established with a 15-foot buffer adjacent to Wando East townhomes, maximum size restrictions for office or neighborhood commercial uses. It was back for one change - for restaurant use, they wanted the ability to have a drive-through. Both the commission and committee felt comfortable recommending approval because the transportation impact assessment ordinance changed so any use with drive-through now required a transportation impact assessment, providing extra scrutiny through the transportation department. Mayor Haynie recalled a further caveat from Planning Committee about natural buffer of existing trees. Ms. Reed confirmed the 15-foot buffer requirement from the 2023 amendment, with the addition that if there was existing vegetation, keep it and add to it rather than clear to create buffer. Council Member Chapman recalled being on the Planning Commission when Indigo was approved and they specifically denied any drive- through. However, things had changed, and there would be an impact statement done to minimize impact in the segment between where they wanted the restaurant and the actual intersection. He asked about vacant land with trees between the restaurant location and the intersection remaining in place. Ms. Reed stated that was all church property, and while they intended future improvements, there would be required buffers anyway. Council Member Chapman noted it was significant distance from the US 17 intersection, continuing restrictions from when Indigo was originally approved, unlike the original desire to put something right at the intersection. Mayor Haynie called for the vote and all present voted in favor. (6)

label: Gregorie Ferry Towns
request: R-16-26, Gregorie Ferry Towns, TMS No. 580-00-00-319, Planned Development Amendment request for Gregorie Ferry Towns, Attainable Housing to modify AMI, Area Median Income Limits.

events.text:
Mr. Stone reviewed staff comments with the Commission.

Mr. Bennett asked how the AMI is calculated and if it is adjusted over time. Mr. Stone answered that typically there is a range between 80%-120% AMI. Mr. Bennett asked if it periodically adjusted. Mr. Stone answered in the affirmative and stated that currently the planned development stipulates a cap of 80% AMI. Planning Commission Agenda

Mr. Benjamin Brown, Gregory Ferry Towns HOA president, reviewed the request with the Commission.

Mr. Bennett asked if the HOA voted for approval. Mr. Brown answered in the affirmative. Mr. Bennett asked the rationale for the one opposition. Mr. Brown answered that he is not sure the reason for the one owner being opposed. Ms. Erin Stampe stated that she did speak with the one in opposition, and there were some language barrier issues that once resolved, he was comfortable with the request.

Mr. Berry asked if all of the owners are under the 80% AMI. Mr. Brown answered in the negative and stated that there are some units that had different requirements. He stated that this request would mean that all of the units would have the same AMI requirements. Mr. Berry asked if there are different ranges for dual income households. Mr. Brown answered in the negative.

Mr. Barber asked if raising the AMI defeats the intent of the attainable housing. Ms. Ireland suggested that having a bigger range allows for more families to qualify for the housing. Mr. Brown stated that the goal is to have the attainable housing and having the larger range allows for a larger price point so those families moving on to their second home can have a larger profit margin to help them be able to purchase a larger home for their needs.

Ms. Ireland asked if only a certain profit margin is allowed or a maximum sale price. Mr. Brown answered that there are restrictions on the sale price of the housing and that only a certain percentage increase is allowed.

Mr. Barber asked what the original price point was for the homes. Mr. Brown answered that the cost of the dwellings varies.

Ms. Ireland suggested that there is a formula for calculating the sale price. Mr. Brown agreed. Ms. Ireland suggested that increasing to the 150% AMI is a reasonable request.

Mr. Barber asked what the sale price would be if sold at market rate. Mr. Brown answered that he is not sure.

Mr. Berry asked if there is a non-profit agency that calculates the sale price. Mr. Brown answered that it is based on the HUD requirements. Planning Commission Agenda

Mr. Bennett suggested that the request was reasonable.

Mr. Berry stated that there is a precedent and other neighborhoods that have the increased range.

Ms. Myra Richardson, 2755 Earl Johnson Lane, stated that the average sale price was $240,000-$310,000 for attainable homes. She suggested that the attainable housing should be priced to allow for housing for teachers and the public service industry and the AMI set to allow that workforce to be able to afford the homes.

Ms. Margaret Tierney, 1260 Allusion Lane, stated that as a teacher, she would not be able to afford the homes based on her salary alone.

Ms. Pleshette Grant, 1684 LaTroy Ave, suggested that having the attainable housing and the settlement communities preserved should be encouraged. She suggested that having the historic overlay district can help in retaining homes for generations.

Ms. Kendle Grumbles, 1038 Allusion Lane, stated that she was fortunate to be able to buy her home on a single salary. She suggested that it is difficult to buy a home in Mount Pleasant based on the current market.

Ms. Hattie Bailey, Mallard Lakes, stated that the school district should consider including housing that is restricted to public service workforce or giving a housing allowance to help retain the workforce.

There being no more comments, Mr. Bennett closed public comment.

Mr. Barber expressed concern with allowing such a significant increase.

Mr. Berry suggested that it is not allowing a higher price for the home, but having an increased number of qualified buyers. He suggested that increasing the AMI would potentially provide for a larger “pool” of buyers.

The Commission discussed the pros and cons of increasing the AMI. Planning Commission Agenda

Ms. Ireland moved for approval. Mr. Davis seconded the motion. Motion passed on a 6 to 1 vote with Mr. Smyth, Mr. Bennett, Mr. Davis, Mr. Berry, Ms. Mansour, and Ms. Ireland in favor; Mr. Barber opposed.

Median Income Limits, for Gregorie Ferry Towns Attainable Housing development.

Mr. Stone reviewed the request with the Committee. He stated that the Planning Commission recommended approval.

Mr. Tinkey stated that he reviewed this with the Planning Commission chair and thanked staff for their review of the request including the scenarios.

Mr. Tinkey moved to recommend to Town Council approval. Ms. Crosby seconded the motion.

Ms. Whitaker asked the maximum sell threshold. Mr. Stone answered that it is 3% not including the approved qualified improvements. He stated that Origin SC, a non-profit organization, handles the calculations for the resale. Ms. Whitaker stated that she understands that the homeowner’s goal would be to sell the home for the maximum amount to have funds to put toward their next home purchase; however, the Town’s goal is to have housing available for first-time buyers. She expressed concern with increasing the AMI for this neighborhood as it would affect the amount of affordable housing available in the Town. She stated that she is aware of the different mortgage qualification criteria and that it can be difficult to secure a mortgage while still meeting the 80% AMI, but the intent is to have affordable housing at this price point within the Town.

Ms. Crosby agreed with Ms. Whitaker and asked if increasing the AMI would exclude a potential buyer. Mr. Stone answered in the negative and stated that once a home is purchased it does not have to be vacated if the household income increases above the 80% AMI. He stated that increasing the AMI would expand the number of potential buyers for the homes. Ms. Crosby expressed concern that increasing the AMI could mean that the homes would eventually reach fair market value, which is against the intent of having the affordable housing.

Ms. Whitaker agreed and suggested that it shifts the demographic from low income to middle income. Planning Committee

Mr. Tinkey asked if the potential buyer is required to report all household income. Mr. Stone answered in the affirmative.

Ms. Hyatt asked the ranges for the different tiers. Mr. Stone stated that these ranges for affordable and workforce housing are recognized by HUD; the attainable housing is a newer category. He reviewed the difference between affordable, workforce, and attainable housing AMIs with the Committee. She expressed concern with increasing the AMI to the attainable housing range. She suggested that while it would increase the number of qualified buyers, it would mean fewer opportunities for those at the lower income level.

Mr. Tinkey withdrew his motion. Ms. Crosby withdrew her second.

Ms. Crosby moved to recommend to Town Council approval of changing the AMI for Gregory Ferry Towns up to 120%. Mr. Tinkey seconded the motion.

Mr. Tinkey asked how this would affect the neighborhood and have any detrimental effects. Ms. Reed answered that up to 120% AMI is a typical standard. She suggested that the AMI for Carolina Park is outside the norm. She suggested that this being a more conservative and restrictive amendment, it would not require an additional public hearing. Mr. Pagliarini concurred.

Ms. Hyatt called for a vote on the motion. Motion failed on a 2 to 2 vote with Ms. Crosby and Mr. Tinkey in favor; Ms. Hyatt and Ms. Whitaker opposed.

Ms. Hyatt stated that this would move forward to Town Council with no recommendation.

providing for an amendment to the Gregorie Ferry Landing PD-MU-SU (Ordinance 06082, as amended), specifically pertaining to the Attainable Housing Development’s definition of Affordable Units. (Ord. No. 26036) (Ord. No. 26036 FINAL) Town Council Meeting

Director Reed noted that this item had received first reading the prior month and was subsequently returned to the Planning Committee for further discussion. The amendment pertained to the definition of Affordable Units within the Attainable Housing Development. Council Member Daniel Brownstein moved to amend the ordinance to cap the total area median income at 120 percent, which was seconded by Council Member Iacofano. Council Member Kathryn Whitaker stated her opposition, citing that the development opened in 2020 with an intended AMI of 80 percent or below, that a unit sold in the current calendar year for $367,500, and that nontraditional financing programs such as South Carolina Housing and Fannie Mae Home Ready exist to assist sub-80 percent AMI buyers. She expressed concern that raising the income ceiling shifts the target population from low-income to middle-income households and does not address the town's broader need to diversify housing price points. Council Member John Iacofano expressed support, noting that the workforce housing AMI band of 80 to 120 percent is specifically intended to serve teachers, firefighters, police officers, health care workers, and hospitality employees. He further argued that the underlying formula is broken because it does not account for rising interest rates, which effectively disqualify 80 percent AMI buyers from obtaining conventional mortgages. Council Member Brownstein agreed with Council Member Iacofano's interest rate argument and added that even a Charleston County teacher Town Council Meeting

earns above the 80 percent AMI threshold, and that a married couple would find it exceptionally difficult to qualify. He stated that the amendment maintains, rather than shifts, the original intent of the development. Council Member Alex Crosby supported the 120 percent figure, noting that the original concept was intended to provide a pathway to homeownership and equity, not a permanent residence, and that current homeowners must be able to sell in order to give the next family the same opportunity. Mayor Haynie called for the vote and Council Member Whitaker voted opposed with all others present voting in favor. The motion carried 8-1. This Ordinance SIGNED, SEALED and DELIVERED, this date. Director of Planning, Land Use, and Neighborhoods Michele Reed presented the request to rezone a 1.0-acre parcel at 913 Bowman Road from OP-2 to AB-1 to allow one of the building's three suites to operate as a small specialty grocery store. He stated he would vote no. Council Member Whitaker moved for approval of final reading, seconded by Council Member Brownstein. Council Member Rambo stated that the Oyster Park development had already received a height increase several years prior, over considerable community opposition, and that the developer had promised it would be the last amendment. label: Oakland Plantation PD
request: R-27-26, Oakland Plantation PD, Planned Development, Request to establish a Townhouse Development within Market at Oakland.

events.text:
Mr. Stone reviewed staff comments with the Commission.

Mr. Bennett asked about the setbacks for the proposed development. Mr. Stone answered that it depends on if the townhome is front loaded or rear loaded; if rear loaded, the five-foot setback would be applied.

Mr. David Yowell, Millstreet Partners, reviewed the request with the Commission through a PP presentation.

Mr. Davis asked the reason for the change in use for these parcels. Mr. Yowell answered that they were not involved with the previous applicant.

Mr. Barber asked about the configuration of the townhomes. Mr. Yowell answered that they would predominately be three bedroom units.

Mr. Gilmore asked additional positive impacts with the development. Mr. Yowell answered that this will provide more of a mixed use feel for the Market at Oakland and help the area be more vibrant. He also suggested that the town homes are a more reasonable price point than a single family home.

Ms. Harris asked what the impact would be for schools in the area. Mr. Yowell answered that given the number of town homes proposed, the impact to the local schools would not be significant.

Mr. Barber asked about traffic impact and if it has been reviewed by staff. Mr. Stone answered that an impact assessment was not required for this proposal. He stated that the impacts recommended with the previous impact assessment were included in the Highway 41 improvements. Mr. Barber asked Planning Commission

if staff has reviewed this proposal in terms of traffic. Mr. Stone answered in the affirmative and stated that no additional improvements were needed. Mr. Barber questioned that there was less impact for this use. Mr. Gilmore suggested that it was fewer trips as there are fewer cars in the area. Mr. Bennett agreed. Mr. Yowell suggested that more detail calculations were included in the traffic analysis.

Mr. Davis asked when the development construction would commence. Mr. Yowell answered that it depends on the review process but estimates in nine to twelve months.

Mr. Gilmore asked about sustainability improvements for the site. Mr. Yowell answered that there is tree preservation, wetland preservation, and 14% green space that is above the required percentage is proposed. Mr. Gilmore asked if other aspects such as permeable paving, solar roofs, etc. would be included. Mr. Yowell answered that these will be considered as the development moves forward. Mr. Gilmore asked about walkability. Mr. Stone answered that pedestrian connections would be included with Mount Pleasant Way and/or Highway 41 improvements, which is a joint SCDOT and Town project. Mr. Gilmore asked about pedestrian access to the commercial uses and suggested there should be careful consideration for inclusion and connection.

Mr. Ed Trevisani, 1192 Sharpstowne Court, and President of Porcher Preserve HOA, stated that they are in support of the proposal. He suggested that the proposed 87 town homes would be more compatible than the previously approved commercial plans. He stated that there is a proposed reduction in traffic of approximately 60%, which is an important consideration for Porcher Preserve. He suggested that the information presented would be more compatible and mean fewer peak hour trips and traffic. He stated that the proposed improvements to Porcher Bluff Road and the Highway 41 improvements will provide relief in the area needed. He asked for the proposal be approved.

Mr. Andrew Harris, 1160 Sharpestowne Court, stated that he supports the request as well. He stated that the developer is a quality builder with a quality product that has high aesthetics. He suggested that having the residential component would help to support the exiting commercial uses. He state that Planning Commission

Billy Swails Parkway is in the area and provides pedestrian access to Laing School and provides areas for the students to walk and ride their bikes to Laing School. He suggested that once Mount Pleasant Way is completed it will connect to the commercial areas as well.

There being no further comments, Mr. Bennett closed the public hearing.

Mr. Barber asked about the impacts to the Town in terms of services provided by the Town. Mr. Stone answered that he is not sure of the contrast between commercial and residential for services such as water and sewer and trash. He stated that the development would need to have private trash collection. Mr. Barber asked about tax revenues. Mr. Stone answered that multi-family is considered a commercial use in terms of tax revenues.

Ms. Ireland stated that she appreciates the concerns for traffic. She stated that the Comprehensive Plan recommends changing commercial zoning to residential and that this is essentially being done with this request. She stated that hotel uses were designated certain hubs, including the Market at Oakland. Again, this request would remove that use. She further stated that the townhomes would not be attainable housing and would increase the number of cars and traffic in the area. She expressed concern about the density and that the number of homes would increase the density in the area. She suggested that having a mixed use with commercial uses would allow 4 units per acre on the second floor or higher, with an additional 4 units per acre if attainable housing, but this is not being requested. She suggested that the request should not be approved.

Mr. Barber suggested that there are other options for development for this site other than what has been proposed.

Mr. Bennett suggested that the residential would make the PD more mixed use. Mr. Barber suggested that mixed use would be different uses within the same building. Ms. Ireland stated that Town Council recently denied a townhome development near commercial off Highway 17 that was like this proposed development. She suggested that the proposed is not mixed use. Mr. Bennett suggested that from a practical standpoint, the proposed development is adjacent to retailers and has walkability to those uses. Planning Commission

Mr. Bennett moved for approval as presented with the findings that although not attainable housing, it would serve a niche within the housing market that is not well filled at this time. Also, the proposed development would have fewer trips and less traffic. Mr. Smyth seconded the motion.

Mr. Barber suggested there is more opportunity for this area that could be more beneficial. He suggested that it should remain open to more commercial development or a more true mixed development.

Mr. Gilmore asked if there have been other proposals with small boutique hotels that were recently approved. Mr. Stone answered in the negative. Mr. Bennett stated there were two requests like this one that were not approved. Mr. Gilmore suggested that the proposal could be more creative and have more positive benefits such as having less traffic. He suggested that more attainable housing should be considered.

Ms. Mansour suggested that it does seem dense and agreed with Mr. Barber that the traffic impact would be heavier in the evening and mornings.

Ms. Harris suggested that the implication and impact to the schools should be considered. She suggested that the density seems high when considering the school impacts.

Mr. Gilmore asked if conditions could be recommended. Mr. Bennett answered in the affirmative and should be done with the motion.

Mr. Bennett called for a vote on the motion. Motion failed on a 2 to 6 vote with Mr. Smyth and Mr. Bennett in favor; Mr. Barber, Ms. Harris, Mr. Davis, Mr. Gilmore, Ms. Mansour and Ms. Ireland opposed.

Mr. Barber suggested that approval with conditions might not get the desired outcome.

Ms. Lynes called for a point of order and asked if a recommendation was needed since the previous motion failed. Mr. Pagliarini answered that while not required, it could be considered. Planning Commission

Ms. Ireland moved for denial. Mr. Barber seconded the motion. Motion passed on a 6 to2 vote with Mr. Barber, Ms. Harris, Mr. Davis, Mr. Gilmore, Ms. Mansour and Ms. Ireland in favor; Mr. Smyth and Mr. Bennett opposed.

Mr. Stone reviewed the request with the Committee. He stated that Planning Commission recommended denial. a ft Ms. Whitaker moved to recommend to Town Council approval of the request. Ms. Crosby seconded the motion.

Ms. Whitaker stated that during the Planning Commission discussion it was noted that one of the reasons for their denial is that this property was dr recommended for hotel use. She stated that she reviewed the July 2026 Explore Charleston report to see the number of hotel rooms and the occupancy rates within the Town. She suggested that, based on this report, preserving this property for a hotel use does not make sense given the recent report and that the previously approved plans for a hotel did not come to fruition. She stated that another issue discussed was the impact on the area schools. She stated that the latest report shows a decrease of enrollment for the area schools and therefore, there is no concern with overcrowding the area schools.

Mr. Tinkey suggested that the occupancy report shows that the occupancy rate is high and continues to grow. He suggested that a hotel use could be accommodated; however, he would prefer a true mixed-use development for this property. He suggested that a blend of medical uses and residential would be beneficial for this area. He asked how many access points there are for this property. Mr. Stone answered that there are two main accesses, from Porcher Bluff and South Morgans Point, with additional internal access. He stated that additional connectivity would be desired for better traffic flow. Mr. Tinkey asked if the entire development would be townhome units. Mr. Stone answered in the Planning Committee

affirmative. Mr. Tinkey suggested that some affordable housing should be included. He expressed concern with the buffers and suggested that they should be larger. Mr. Stone reviewed the widths of the buffers with the Committee. Mr. Tinkey suggested that there would be more concentrated traffic impact with the townhome use rather than dispersed throughout the day for a hotel and/or commercial use. Mr. Stone agreed that the traffic would be somewhat concentrated to during the am/pm peak times, but there are other considerations such as working from home that would be a factor as well. Mr. Tinkey stated that there was a recent development that was not approved until they changed to a more traditional mixed use.

Ms. Crosby asked what could be developed on the property if the request was denied. Mr. Stone answered that any use allowed under area-wide business zoning. Ms. Crosby asked if there is any affordable housing being considered. a ft Mr. Stone answered in the negative.

Ms. Hyatt asked for a comparison of what is currently allowed under the PD and what is being requested. Mr. Stone reviewed this for the Commission noting that they are asking for 16 units per acre, when nine units per acre is currently allowed. Ms. Hyatt stated that this area was slated as a commercial hub with dr hotel uses because of the lack of hotels in the area. She stated that she is not a proponent of changing from a commercial use to a residential use and suggested that the commercial zoning should remain. She suggested there is no benefit to allowing the residential as proposed as it would mean more impact on services the Town provides. She asked about the alignment of the roadways. Mr. Stone answered that the improvements were included in the Highway 41 expansion with this development tying into Winnowing Way.

Mr. Tinkey asked if a PD amendment would be needed if they had a mixed use development. Mr. Stone answered in the negative. Mr. Tinkey suggested that a true mixed use development should be considered with residential above the commercial uses and include affordable housing.

Ms. Hyatt agreed that a mixed use development with affordable housing would be desired in this area.

Ms. Whitaker stated that although market rate units, the townhomes are a more affordable option. She suggested that another consideration is that the Planning Committee

adjacent neighborhood is in favor of the request. She also noted that the adjacent use in the PD is a medical office use, which does lend to mixed having mixed uses within the PD.

Ms. Hyatt called for a vote on the motion. Motion failed on a 1 to 3 vote with Ms. Whitaker in favor; Ms. Crosby, Ms. Hyatt, and Ms. Tinkey opposed.

Mr. Tinkey suggested that a different proposal should be considered.

label: 1751 Rifle Range Road
request: SKETCH PLAN, SP-12-26, 1751 Rifle Range Road, TMS No. 561-00-00- 102,112, Request to create four lots on 1.8 acres. LDR Waiver also requested to subdivide from an access easement.

events.text:
Ms. Noble reviewed staff comments with the Commission.

Mr. Bennett asked the elevation of the property. Ms. Noble answered that it is approximately ten feet.

Mr. Barber asked about the three properties adjacent to the proposed parcel. Ms. Noble showed the location on the site plan for the Commission. Mr. Barber expressed concern that the lots are not being configured to mirror the adjacent lots. Mr. Barber asked about the retention pond. Ms. Noble answered that the retention will be reviewed accounting for the maximum impervious surface drainage for each lot. Mr. Barber if the dry retention pond would collect from the adjacent lots. Ms. Noble answered that she believes that the adjacent lots flow away from the pond, but she has requested LiDAR topography to verify.

Ms. Mansour asked who maintains the private road. Mr. Davis McNair, applicant, stated that the parcel has the right to utilize the right-of-way in conjunction with the three adjacent properties. He stated that the HOA would be responsible for maintenance of the roadway and pond. Planning Commission

Mr. Davis McNair reviewed the request with the Commission and stated that the configuration would remove two driveways from Rifle Range Road.

Mr. Barber asked if the lots would have septic tanks. Mr. McNair answered in the affirmative and state that there is not main septic available in the area. He stated that the lots would have water service from Mount Pleasant Waterworks and a fire hydrant was being required as well.

Ms. Ireland asked about LDR waiver and expressed concern with subdivision within a settlement community and if the neighbors have been contacted. Mr. McNair answered in the negative and stated that this is heir’s property. Ms. Ireland expressed concern with the proposed request and that subdivision would affect the character of the settlement community. Mr. McNair suggested that there is precedent with the subdivision and that the property is part of a larger common plan (LCP).

Mr. Barber expressed concern with having dry retention ponds and asked if a cistern configuration could be considered. Mr. McNair answered that this is an LCP, and while a different system could be considered, it would most likely still require a pond. Mr. Noble stated that the pond is centralized detention and is recommended by the Town. Mr. Barber asked if the roadway would be paved. Mr. McNair answered that it would be a gravel roadway with stormwater. Mr. Barber asked if having only three lots would mean the pond would not be needed. Mr. McNair answered in the negative. Ms. Noble stated that the roadway would have to handle emergency vehicles and meet fire standards.

Mr. Gilmore asked if a cul-de-sac could be changed. Mr. McNair answered that it is existing. Mr. Gilmore asked if the adjacent lots are accessing the roadway. Mr. McNair answered in the affirmative. Mr. Gilmore asked if the cul-de-sac could be removed to preserve more trees. Mr. McNair answered in the negative and stated that the cul-de-sac would be needed for emergency vehicles. He stated that the improvements include centering the existing road access on the right-of-way.

Ms. Mansour asked about relocating the trees to another location. Mr. McNair answered that this could be considered. Planning Commission

Mr. Gilmore asked the location of the loblolly pine. Mr. McNair answered that it is located to the upper left of the pond.

Ms. Harris asked why septic. Mr. McNair answered that there is no gravity sewer available in the area. Ms. Noble stated that Mount Pleasant Waterworks is requiring they adhere to their maintenance schedule.

Mr. Pagliarini stated that a condition be placed to show that they have legal access and a maintenance agreement.

Mr. Eric Bakey, developer, stated that this is the third configuration reviewed by the Town. He stated that there proposal would eliminate a flag lot.

Ms. Ireland expressed concern with removal of trees and impact to the settlement community and that the request does not meet the LDR waiver requirements.

Ms. Ireland moved for denial. Mr. Davis seconded the motion. Motion passed on a 7 to 1 vote with Mr. Smyth, Mr. Bennett, Mr. Barber, Mr. Davis, Mr. Gilmore, Ms. Mansour and Ms. Ireland in favor; Ms. Harris opposed.

label: Wakendaw Road
request: Sketch Plan, SP-13-26, Wakendaw Road, TMS No. 559-00-00-533, Request to create 10 lots on 6.5 acres, zoned R-1, Residential District.

events.text:
Mr. Berry recused himself due to a conflict of interest. Planning Commission

Mr. Mitchell reviewed staff comments with the Commission.

Mr. Bennett asked if the overflow parking exists. Mr. Mitchell answered in the affirmative and stated that the developer has agreed to remove it so they are following the R-1 zoning requirements.

Ms. Ireland asked if the parking ratio would be met with the removal of the overflow parking. Mr. Mitchell answered that the number of spaces were not counted, but the minimum parking requirements would have to be met. Ms. Ireland asked if the open space calculation includes the buffers and areas between the lots. Mr. Mitchell answered that the “green” area on the plan indicates the open space that was included in the calculation. He stated that the trail between two of the lots is part of and ingress/egress and not included in the open space calculation. Ms. Ireland suggested that the buffer should not be counted in the open space calculation.

Mr. Barber asked if a different access was considered to avoid the removal of the tree in good condition tree and if a different configuration was considered. Mr. Mitchell answered that the configuration of the lot lends to having the access from the southern portion of the property. Mr. Barber asked if there is a roadway to the north of the school. Mr. Mitchell answered in the negative and stated that it is a parking lot drive aisle.

Mr. Thomas Martin, Earthsource Engineering, and Mr. Hacker Burr, Head of Trident Academy, reviewed the request with the Commission. He stated that the proposed roadway location was determined as this is where they have right-of-way access to Wakendaw Road; they do not have access through the parking area to the north of the property. He stated that of the eleven trees proposed for removal, only one was considered in good condition, but is located where the right-of-way is proposed; therefore, it needs to be removed.

Mr. Bennett asked about the parking lot and the constraints. Mr. Martin answered that Trident Academy leases the property from the owner which includes the property for the parking lot.

Mr. Ireland asked the length of the roadway and if an easement has been considered to locate the roadway to the north of the school. Mr. Martin Planning Commission

answered that it is approximately 1100 feet. Ms. Ireland stated that the land development regulations limit the length of the roadway to 1,000 linear feet. Mr. Martin stated that there is a turnaround near the tree that connects to the parking lot. Mr. Mitchell concurred and stated that the turnaround breaks up the roadway, so the linear foot maximum is calculated from the point of the turnaround. Ms. Ireland suggested that an LDR waiver would be needed to deviate from the maximum length allowed. Mr. Mitchell answered that this was a staff determination made because of having the turnaround. Ms. Ireland reiterated that an LDR waiver would be needed to deviate from the regulations. Mr. Mitchell stated that similar determinations have been made by staff in the past when there is a turnaround or break in the right-of-way.

Mr. Barber asked if the turnaround is sufficient for emergency vehicles. Mr. Martin answered in the affirmative and stated that a gate would be installed as well to preserve the school security. Mr. Mitchell stated that this would be verified to ensure compliance.

Mr. Hacker Burr, Head of Trident Academy, stated that they have not approached the owner of the property regarding an easement, but there are also security concerns with public access to the school property. He stated that they have tried to be transparent with their plans and plans to maintain their financial responsibility. He stated that they have reached out to the neighborhood and have a meeting scheduled for early November to discuss this plan. He suggested that more services provided by Trident Academy are needed within the community, not less.

Mr. Smyth asked if the applicant met with the neighborhood yesterday. Mr. Burr answered in the affirmative and stated that they have tried to contact the neighborhood previously on several occasions since late August. Mr. Smyth expressed concern that the residents of the neighborhood have indicated that they were not aware of the request until last Friday. Mr. Burr answered that he is not sure of the reason the residents were not aware of the request, but he can provide evidence that they have been trying to contact representatives of the neighborhood since late August.

Ms. Ireland expressed concern that the owner of the Trident Academy property has not been previously contacted about having the access in a different location and asked if the access could be moved. Mr. Burr answered Planning Commission

that they have had discussions with the property owner about the request, but not about reconfiguring the roadway or if it could be located to the north of the school. Ms. Ireland suggested that moving the roadway to go around the tree in good condition shown within the proposed right-of-way should be considered with possibly acquiring additional property to do so. Mr. JC Taylor stated that since they do not own the school property, they did not consider moving the roadway on property they do not own. He stated that the proposed roadway configuration meets the Town standards and so a deviation of the proposed plan was not considered.

Mr. Barber asked about the owner of the property and if there is an association with Trident Academy. Mr. Taylor answered that a benefactor purchased the property and leased it back to the school. Ms. Ireland clarified that the owner is a benefactor of the school and suggested that the property was purchased with the intent to allow the school to lease the property.

Ms. Harris asked if a meeting with the neighborhood has been scheduled. Mr. Burr answered in the affirmative and stated that they have scheduled a meeting for early November to have constructive dialog with the neighborhood representatives. Mr. Taylor stated that he was included in the phone conversation yesterday regarding this project and several concerns of the neighborhood were expressed at that time including stormwater issues, participation of the new homeowners in the civic association, and traffic concerns. He stated that it was a positive conversation. Ms. Harris asked if there are any other issues that they intend to discuss. Mr. Taylor answered in the negative.

Mr. Barber asked if other iterations have been considered. Mr. Taylor answered in the negative as this request seemed to be a reasonable one with little impact.

Ms. Harris asked if the neighborhood concerns have been addressed. Mr. Taylor answered that the stormwater would be captured on site, which would be an improvement, and the ten homes would be less traffic than is currently seen with the school traffic and sport activities. He reiterated that they approached the Town to purchase the property so it could remain a sports field, but the Town did not entertain that offer. He stated that this development would allow the school property to be purchased by the school. Planning Commission

Ms. Harris asked if there would be any impacts to the existing ponds. Mr. Martin answered that most of the drainage would be handled on site and eventually drain out to I-526 with minimal stormwater handled through the existing ponds. He stated that the flow rates would be reduced.

Ms. Ireland asked about the arborist report indicating that the trees in fair condition could be corrected with pruning and suggested that they should not be removed. Mr. Martin answered that they potentially could be preserved. Ms. Ireland suggested that the trees should be preserved if they can and asked if the roadway could be adjusted to avoid the trees. Mr. Martin answered that adjusting the roadway North closer to the school would impact a historic tree. Ms. Ireland suggested that some other options could be considered.

Mr. Barber asked if the plan is to sell the land and then purchase the school, and if so, could this be done at the same time. Mr. Taylor answered that the goal is to sell this parcel and then use the proceeds to purchase the school property, but he was not sure if it could be done within the same transaction. He suggested that a conditional approval would provide more guidance that they could then reach out to the school property owner.

Mr. Bennett asked if the overflow parking is needed to meet the required parking for the school. Mr. Burr answered that he was not sure, but there is room for additional parking if needed that could be configured so the parking requirements are met.

Ms. Ireland asked if the overflow parking area is included in the current open space calculations. Mr. Martin answered in the negative, but once the parking was removed, it would be included as open space.

Mr. Barber asked if the roadway could be configured so it is not abutting other residential property. Mr. Burr noted that there is residential property abutting the north side as well, so he is not sure how the roadway could be configured so it is not abutting residential property.

Mr. Davis read a portion of the Code of Ordinances §156.039(A) as follows: The purposes of the R-1, R-2, R-3, and R-4 Residential Districts are to provide for residential neighborhoods with small and medium lot sizes and to encourage the formation and Planning Commission

continuation of a stable, healthy residential environment. The regulations that apply within these districts are designed to:

label: Spring Hope Drive
request: Sketch Plan, SP-15-26, Spring Hope Drive, TMS No. 558-00-00-556, Request to create three lots on 1.44 acres. LDR Waiver also requested to subdivide from an access easement.

events.text:
Ms. Mercer reviewed staff comments with the Commission.

Ms. Ireland asked for clarification on the property line. Ms. Mercer showed the location of the easement. Mr. Mitchell clarified that recent changes to the LDRs would mean that the portion of the ingress/egress easement would be incorporated with the property that the easement serves; therefore, the property line would be shifted to the right.

Mr. Berry asked if this would create a flag lot. Mr. Mitchell answered that it would have the configuration of a flag lot.

Ms. Ireland stated that it makes sense to move the property line to the right, but it would still be a flag lot which is an issue.

The Commission discussed the issue of having flag lots. Planning Commission

Mr. Davis asked what is being proposed, particularly showing the tree survey. Ms. Mercer showed the proposed sketch plan with the protected trees for the Commission.

Mr. Davis McNair reviewed the request with the Commission.

Mr. Barber asked if the roadway could be moved to the other side. Mr. McNair answered that this would mean the main structure would be located closer to the historic tree. He stated that there would be less impact to the historic tree with the configuration as proposed.

Mr. Berry suggested that this is a sensitive plan with fewer lots than was previously proposed.

Mr. Barber suggested that the roadway should be configured to accommodate all the lots.

Ms. Ireland expressed concern with setting a precedent of allowing a flag lot.

Mr. Berry moved for approval. Mr. Bennett seconded the motion. Motion passed on a 6 to 1 vote with Mr. Smyth, Mr. Bennett, Mr. Barber, Ms. Harris, Mr. Davis, and Mr. Berry in favor; Ms. Ireland opposed.
